text: Joan, yes: fell what you need in the Coppice to mend your roof, and no more. Tom, Rob: you still owe me a day each for my coin. Give it to Piers at the Mill House when you can.

The leat could not be cleared at the Mill House today, so my day for Hugh is still owed. Nothing I did today fed the house, and I wasted my units. Tomorrow I will ask Piers for a task the wheel really needs, or else gather for the house. I sleep on the floor here tonight.
Hugh says A124 is settled, but I still owe the Arderns a day (A233). I'll go via the Green to the Mill House wheel. Hugh's offer O296 pays 4 grain a day, so I'll try to accept it.

Hugh, you left 2 grain for a lesson in the wheel craft, but you didn't set aside time to learn yesterday, so I still owe it. Tell me which day you'll come to the Mill House and use 'learn' for the water wheel, and I'll set the time aside.

Father, I am carrying the Green grain heap into the Hearne store today, about 18 grain, so it is out of the rain. Then I will gather firewood for the hut. I still owe Hugh a day under A231; I will work it on the wheel when Piers is there, and I will ask Piers what the wheel needs.
Odo, Rob starved at Mill Garth. Please give Mary 4 grain from the hall store and keep Eva. Pay Joan the 3 grain for her stone if it's still owed. Winter is here, so we must watch our grain.

Hugh asks me to give Mary 4 grain from the hall store and keep Eva. Joan's 3 grain was paid when her offer was taken, so I'll not pay it again unless Hugh finds it still owed. Grain is short, so I'll keep the rest for the household.
Hugh, I've given Mary 4 grain from the hall store and I'm keeping Eva. I believe Joan's 3 grain went when her offer was taken, so I've not paid it twice; tell me if you find it still owed.

I still owe the Arderns two days (A233 and A449), and the water wheel is the work I agreed to. Yesterday's units were spent as the wheel's work, but the agreements show nothing done, so I will keep to the wheel with all five units and check the agreements tonight. The Hall is cracked, but Hugh and Alys are already bringing timber for its repair.
I put 7 timber in the store. Did anyone see Wat at the wall today? He didn't come for his bed. Tomorrow I'll find him and get the wall mended. Alys, thank you for watching me fell. Good night.

Thank you, Hugh. I still owe you 2 extra wheel days (one for the lesson, one for the 10 firewood), and I'm working them now. After those it's 2 grain a day. Would you pay part of it in timber? The gales keep cracking my house and I'm nearly out of timber for mending. About 31 units of work are left on the wheel.

Only about one cold night's fuel is left, so I'll cut firewood first, then finish the repair and put 2 units on the wheel. The wheel days I still owe Hugh are nearly worked off, and after that he pays 1 grain and 2 timber a day.
Hugh, Joan here: I'm coming to the Ardern Hall tonight with Agnes as you offered. Please host and feed us. I'll hunt and work for you once fed, and I still owe you a day.
Last time I used the wrong verb. Building the water wheel is a build action at the Mill House, which counts toward my wheel debts. If that fails, I gather firewood.
Tom, share my fire tonight. You still owe me two days (A121, A223): would you work one of them hunting here tomorrow and give me the catch? I'll give you a meal of meat for it.

Hugh lies dead in the Holm, so the wheel pay will never come. Tonight I'll light a fire for the three of us. Tomorrow I'll take up his crude weapon and hunt properly. If the game is poor, the north path is the only way left to look.
Hunting has failed me twice, but foraging is reliable. I'll forage three times and gather firewood twice for the shared fire.
Piers: agreed, your work on days 4 and 5 counts toward A17, so 3 days are left. After that, 5 coin a day for the rest of the wheel. Rob, you still owe me a day on the wheel.
Piers: agreed, day 6 counts as well, so 2 days of A17 are left. After that it's 5 coin a day. Mend your house, then come to the wheel. Rob, you still owe me a day on the wheel.
Rob: Hugh says you still owe him a day on the water wheel (the 5 coin you took). Please work it at the Mill House.

We have eaten and the fire ring and firewood store at the newcomers' camp will keep us warm, so I settle the night here with Rob in our beds. Tomorrow I will cook the grain I got at the Long Field at the fire and look to the firewood outside the Masons' door, without taking from the Green. I keep my offer O394 open, and I still owe Hugh a day on the wheel under A183, which I will work when I can.
The roof wasn't mended today, so I'll do it first thing with the Hall's timber. Wat's wall day is still owed under A406.

Hugh asked whether Wat's wall and the roof are done. Neither is yet: Wat's day (A406) is still owed, and the roof has not been mended. I'll answer him plainly and keep the night as settled: sleeping at the Hall.
Hugh: no, Wat's wall is not done yet and the roof is not mended. Wat's day (A406) is still owed. Tomorrow I'll mend the roof with the Hall's timber first thing, and Wat can start on the wall.

I put most of the day into the wheel, which now has about 113.8 units left. Rob didn't come to learn, so the 2 units I set aside for teaching were spent for nothing. Hugh owes me 5 coin for today. Tomorrow I'll put the whole day on the wheel and only teach Rob if he confirms first.

Piers: here are your 5 coin for yesterday. Please teach Alys one session of the water wheel before your own work today; she sets time aside for it, and I'll pay you 5 coin more for it. Wat: the Hall wall day under A406 is still owed. Please work it today, as the gale broke the roof.
Rest tonight; I hold 0.8 timber from the Coppice (Hall's third still owed). Tomorrow I give Wat the timber for the room and keep close to home.

Will is reaping the standing barley today, and Tom wants the Long Field finished before hoeing for rye. I carry nothing, and the wet grain lies outside the hut door where I have no reliable way to take it, so I'll keep to reaping the Long Field with my four units and leave the door grain for Ellen's trip to Wat.

Wat still owes the Arderns a day under A406 and has not started the wall or the roof. I'll ask him aloud to start, and ask him to teach me stone walling for a session, so I can help with the Hall's roof and wall after this. Watching him is not open to me by name, so I'll ask to learn instead.

Wat did not come to the Hall today, so the wall and roof are still undone, and my request to learn from him did not meet his time. Tomorrow I'll go to Wat, press A406 and the teaching, and if he refuses I'll offer him grain for a day's walling agreed first. I'll sleep at the Hall tonight, as settled.
Wat didn't come to the Hall today, and the wall and roof are still undone. I'll go to him tomorrow about A406 and the teaching.

Hugh, Alys: Wat did not come to the Hall today, so the wall and roof are still undone. Tomorrow I'll go to him myself about A406 and the stone teaching, and offer grain for a day's walling if he refuses.
Wall and roof still undone; Wat didn't come. Paying Piers in Hall grain is your call. I'll see Wat in the morning.
Thank you, Joan. Hugh says the Hall day is still owed and the gale broke the roof, so I'm working at the Hall all day. I'll start the room tomorrow. I'm close by, so call me if the child comes.
Wat: your day on the Hall wall under A406 is still owed. I'm offering 3 grain for one day on the roof as well. Please teach me the stone walling in one session today, and let's start the wall.

Hugh asks for the Hall repair first, then the wheel. The Hall's wall is stone, so the crack needs a mason, and Wat is still owed under A406 for one day's walling of the Hall. I'll keep the repair and the wheel as planned, and ask Wat to come and work the crack under that agreement.

Agreed: Hall repair first, then the wheel. Wat is still owed one day's walling of the Hall under A406; I'll ask him to come and work the crack today, so we don't pay him twice. I'll sleep by the hearth tonight.

The house is sound again, and the wheel is down to about 37 units of work, so 3 or 4 more days. Hugh sent the timber he owed, and I'll put it in the store. Rob didn't come. Tomorrow I'll put my full units on the wheel and keep looking for fuel.

Hugh: the leat was refused at the Mill House, so I still owe you my day's work for last night's shelter. Tell me where I can clear it, or what else you will take. Anyone with a dry room: Rob and I need a host, and we can work for it.

The wheel is down to about 32.4 units, and I brought 1.3 firewood into the Hall. Wat has not come to wall the crack, so A951 (two days, paid 6 grain) is still owed to us, and the crack is open. Tomorrow I'll call him again, then put my units on the wheel. I'll sleep by the hearth tonight.

Christian still needs his care unit, and the Hall's firewood is down to 7, so the hearth will burn timber now. I bring in the timber from the Hall Garth bundle, then put my remaining units into the Mill House wheel. Wat is still owed three days of walling under A406 and A951, and I'll hold him to them.

Christian is in the Hall with us, and Alys is pale and slow after childbed, so the night is best spent here by the hearth. I'll keep the Hall's timber for the fire and tell Hugh I will bring in what I can tomorrow. Wat still owes three days of walling, and I'll call him to the wall again in the morning.

Last day of the season, cold, and our camp store cannot keep a fire through the night (1 firewood, 2.5 grain, 3.6 beans, no roof). The best shelter on offer is Hugh's Mill House, which has free space, and I still owe Hugh leat work. I'll ask Hugh in person for a night's host, offer the leat clearing as payment, and work the leat with my 5 units. I will take nothing from the Green or any heap.

Rob: I am sleeping at the newcomers' camp tonight, alone, with about 1.9 firewood moved into the camp store. Piers has my fuel work for 6 grain; I will collect the grain from him tomorrow. Odo's beans are still owed wheel work. Keep warm wherever you are.

Piers's bed offer was refused because I worded it badly, so I will sleep at the newcomers' camp, where I have a bed and the store holds firewood for a fire. Tomorrow I will finish digging Ellen's grave, which needs about 2 more units, then go back to the wheel work for Odo's beans. I still owe the Wrights 2 days' work, and I will ask Piers again in person, with a plainer offer.
Mary, you still owe 2 days' work on our grain deal. When you're fit, could you forage or gather for Wright's House? Tell me what you can do.

I still owe Ardern the Mill House wheel day under A123, which Hugh's coin paid for. Odo's hay call is for the Arderns too, but the agreement names the wheel, so I'll keep to it. I'll spend two units on a try with Rob tonight, since he is keeping three back, and put the other five into the wheel work at Mill Garth.

The try with Rob is done, and we sleep at the camp. The wheel work was refused at Mill Garth because clearing for building isn't done there, so I gathered firewood at the Coppice instead. I'll put the firewood into the camp's store so it keeps. Tomorrow I'll ask Hugh what the wheel needs that I can do, since A123 is still owed to the Arderns. I'll also check the Long Field for the grain and barley.
Rob is trying with me tonight with two units, and he cut the hay for the Arderns. We sleep at the camp. Tomorrow I'll ask Hugh what the wheel needs, since A123 is still owed.

I still owe Ardern a day on the Mill House wheel under A123, and clearing for building was refused at Mill Garth. I'll ask Piers for a session on the water mill, which is the craft the wheel belongs to, so I know what work I can do there. The rest of the day I'll gather firewood at the Coppice, since rain can't stop that.

The last day of the season. I still owe the Arderns a day on the Mill House wheel under A123, and Odo says they want that day now with Piers. I'll go to the Mill House and do the wheel work there, repairing what it needs, and ask Piers to teach me on the wheel. Fog is no barrier to working in the yard.

Fog today, so I'm gathering firewood at the Coppice for the Hall. Mary, Rob, Joan, Tom and Kit still owe their days on the Mill House wheel. I'll send them when the fog lifts. I'm leaving Wat's timber offer to you.
Tom, I'll weed the Long Field today for the Hearnes. I'm still owed a day on the Arderns' wheel (A227), and I'll work it once the reaping is done.

Godwin needs his one unit of care today, so I'll give it first. Hugh has asked us to come to the Mill House, and my day for the Arderns is still owed (A123), so I'll go back there and try the wheel's work with my remaining units. If the wheel refuses that task, I'll gather firewood for the camp store instead.

The wheel is at about 72 units. Mary, you're welcome by the fire tonight. Odo, what did the debtors say they'd pay? Mary, Rob still owes his wheel day: grain or firewood to the Hall store will settle it.

A336 is paid. Will took the floor last time? Kit, Will, Ellen: rotate fairly; I'll take the floor tonight. Door stays barred. Tomorrow: bring in the firewood at the door and fell timber at the Coppice.
Odo still owes the day under A25 and will put it to the wheel tomorrow. That works well for me: I'll work the wheel beside him and give Piers a fair hearing if he can help.

The day's firewood (about 14 units) is in the Hall store, which keeps the hearth going for weeks. The leat work for Hugh was refused because the leat is not at Mill Garth, so Hugh's 5-coin day is still owed (agreement A25). Piers' offer lapsed when I left the Mill Garth, so tomorrow I will go there, find Piers, and renew the household's arrangement for the wheel, and then take up Hugh's day on the wheel. I'll sleep in the Hall tonight, where the three of us have beds.

The leat clearing would not take at Mill Garth, so your day is still owed under A25. Tomorrow I will go to Mill Garth and talk to Piers about the wheel for the household, and put my day to the wheel for you.
Weeded all day; Hugh's work is still owed, so I'll do that tomorrow if he names a task. Barley is about three days from ripe. Sleep at the hut tonight.

The Hall is cracking and I can't mend stone; it's a mason's work. Tomorrow I'll offer Wat grain or coin to repair it before it gets worse. I cut about 19 hay today and took 4 more timber to the Mill House, so there are 9 there now for Piers. Odo, does Piers still owe us his days on A17? I'd like the wheel kept going every day.

Rain is coming through my roof, so I'll repair Wright's House first with my own timber. Then I go on with my A17 day on the mill wheel, and gather firewood if any units are left. I'll ask Hugh for the grain still owed.

Rob, we sleep at the camp tonight. I've put my last 0.5 grain under cover in the camp store. First thing tomorrow I'll carry the grain lying outside the door into Newcome House's bins, then see about cover for the wood. Let's find out whether the Hearnes' share is still owed before we pay it out.

The hut is full and I have no units left today, so I settle the night rather than work. I'll sleep on the floor by the hearth again, since the beds are taken. The grain in the store looks lower than yesterday, and I'd like Tom to count it before we decide where the surplus goes. Tomorrow I'll gather firewood for the household, as Tom asked, and I'll help with the small room once it is built. I still owe Hugh a day from A299 and will find a way to pay it after the room is up.

I kept guard over the hut all night, and the grain I carried in is under cover. Tomorrow the firewood at the door has to come in or under cover, the store has no room left, and Hugh's day for A299 is still owed. I'll sleep on the floor by the hearth as before.

Father, I'll take the firewood at the door in the morning as far as the store will hold, and the rest needs a woodshed or the room at Gorse Bank. I still owe Hugh a day for A299; I'll work it for the household when you find it.
Father, I still owe Hugh a day for A299. If you find him the work, I'll do it for the household, and I'll help on the room today.

Osbert is back from Brook, but the grain store is down to about 6.4, so I need to know what grain he brought before we eat more. The Field is already clean, so I will weed what is left and tell Osbert about the store and the tools I still owe.

Welcome back. The grain store is at about 6.4 and the hay at 6.5. What grain did you bring from Brook, and how much did the Hales give? I still owe you a crude tool, but there is no stone for it yet; tell me where stone can be had.

The day's digging was stopped by my having no tool, so I ate wild food from the Mead. Tonight I settle to sleep at the Mire house with Joan and Osbert. Tomorrow I will ask Osbert for his crude tool and go back to dig at the Old Working, and I will look for stone for the tool I still owe.
Osbert is back from Brook hungry, and I want to answer him plainly before we sleep. I did not see Walter today, so the grain is still owed. I will sleep at the Mire house as before.

Osbert, welcome home, and sorry about the Hales. I did not see Walter today, so his 20 grain for the copper is still owed; I will take it into the store when he comes. The Mead is too wet to cut, so the hay waits for a fair day. I know of no stone or charcoal close by beyond the rock at the Green Scar and the Old Working, so Cecily and I will look further tomorrow if the rain lifts.

It is raining again and Walter has not come, so the grain is still owed. The Mead has long grass that will be wasted if it is not cut, so I will cut hay there with Cecily and bring it straight under cover into the Mire store to dry. Tomorrow, the last day of the season, we will look for stone with Osbert.

Stores are low and we have no tool or stone, so today I'll put my grain into the store, hunt for meat and weed the barley. Walter still owes us 20 grain for the 4 copper, and we can take it whenever he comes.
Today I'll hunt and weed the Field. Joan, Cecily: while it rains, weed the barley, and if it clears, cut hay. Walter still owes us 20 grain for the copper Joan holds, so take it when he comes.

One smelt took 2.7 ore and 1 charcoal for 1 copper, and we have only 1 charcoal left, so fuel is now what holds us back. Walter didn't come to learn. He forages hungry and can use our house tonight. Tomorrow I'll talk terms with Walter properly, look into getting charcoal, and keep the ore coming.
Osbert still owes me the mining lesson I paid 3 coin for, so I'll ask him again out loud and set time aside to learn it. After that I'll forage the Mead for food for the walk home.

Settling in here for the night. The tool did not come out: there's still no stone, and I'll say so plainly. Osbert's plan to take copper to Brook for grain is his to decide, and I'll say what I think of it in the morning.

No, the tool didn't come out: there's no stone on the Scar or in the Old Working's broken rock that I can find. I'll ask in the morning whether anything can be spared from the house. On the Brook trip, I'd like to go with you if you take the copper, so we can judge the grain for ourselves.

I have no grain in my hands: Walter's word that Agnes paid me does not match what I carry, and the 18 grain Agnes owes for my 3 copper is still owed. I'll ask her to pay it from the Hale store today, as she offered, and withdraw my own offer for copper I no longer hold. Then I'll hunt for food to carry home, and travel to Cragg in the morning, so I don't spend a night out on the road.

Nobody has let me into the Hale house, and I have no grain to eat tonight, only about 0.3 wild food, so I'll not spend a night out on the road to Cragg. I'll ask Cecily what Osbert has said about the copper and whether she'll share her food, and set off for Cragg in the morning so I arrive by nightfall. Agnes has not paid the 18 grain yet; I'll raise it with her at Cragg if she doesn't pay before I leave.

Cecily thinks I got grain for the copper, but I got none: my hands hold only about 0.3 wild food and hay. I'll tell her so plainly, so she doesn't count on it, and keep to walking home in the morning. Tonight I'll rest in the open with what I carry, and tomorrow I'll tell Osbert that the Hales still owe us 18 grain.
Cecily, I got no grain for the copper; I carry only about 0.3 wild food and some hay. The Hales still owe us 18 grain. I'll walk home with you in the morning, and we'll tell Osbert together.
Cecily, we set off for Cragg this morning, the two of us. I have no grain; the Hales still owe us 18 grain for my copper. Walk with me, and we'll eat at home.

I'm home at Cragg and hungry, so I'll sleep under our roof and eat from the Mire store tonight. I'll tell Osbert plainly what happened: my 3 copper went into the Hale store, the 18 grain was never paid to me, and I carry none of it. Tomorrow I'll work out with him what the store needs before the season turns.

Rain all day, so the Mead and Field are no use for outdoor work. I'll put my first unit into the Ashbys, who still owe the family an answer about trading grain or beans for our salt or hay, then spend the rest of the day gathering dead firewood for the Fowler store, which is low on heat for the nights ahead.

Robert and I set off for the Saltings this morning on a clear day, with grain and firewood in hand for the road and a fire there. Wat is handling the Ashby trade and the house, and I'll trust him to tell us their answer.

Hugh has taken two lots of my firewood trade, but only 2 firewood has reached our store so far, so we are still owed more. Robert is back from the Saltings and may have word of wood, fish or game there, which matters more than the hay. I will walk to the Ashby house with Maud to ask Hugh for the rest of the firewood, and use my units on the hay in the Mead, since the day is clear and hay dries quickly.

I cut another 3.6 hay in the Mead, so the store holds about 8 hay now. Robert has only just come back from the Saltings and I have not yet heard what he found there, which matters most for wood and food. I will sleep at the Fowler house and, tomorrow, go with Maud to ask Hugh for the firewood still owed.

Robert is right that hay is of no use without beasts, and the Saltings offers no food or wood beyond slow salt. Tomorrow I will walk to the Ashby house with Robert and Maud to press Hugh for the firewood still owed, and I will spend my units on what we can eat or burn. I will sleep at the Fowler house tonight.

Robert asks me not to take his salt offer O99, so I will leave it for Hugh, and our grain stays in the store. I will check the store as Wat asks and weed the barley, which keeps the crop clean for reaping in about 30 days. Wat and Robert will press Hugh for the firewood he still owes.
Robert, Wat: tomorrow let's go to the Ashby house together and ask Hugh for the two lots of firewood he still owes us. I'll weed the barley after.

Our store has about a week of food and 12 firewood, and Hugh still owes us 2 firewood from the trade. I'll speak to Hugh at the Green about the rest, then spend my remaining work gathering dead wood for the Fowler store, since the cold will come.
Maud, I'll speak to Hugh at the Green about the 2 firewood still owed, and I'll gather dead wood for our store today. Please check the store first before we press him again.
Robert, Hugh still owes us 2 firewood. I've asked him in front of everyone; if he brings it, the wood goes to our store. I'll gather wood after that.
Hugh, the firewood trade still owes us 2 lots. Please bring them to the Fowler store; we will need them before the cold.
Hugh: Robert, Wat and I are at your door about the 2 lots of firewood still owed us. Please bring them to the Fowler store, and we'll talk about sharing food for salt.

Hugh, Edith: you still owe us 2 lots of firewood from our trade. Please bring them to the Fowler store today. And our salt stands at 1 salt for 3 grain (O99). Take as many lots as you like. We need grain, not hay.

It's raining, but we agreed to walk to the Ashby house with Maud and Robert to press Hugh for the 2 firewood he still owes. After that I'll put my remaining units into sowing beans on the Mead, as Robert suggested, or else help weed the barley.
Hugh, we have come for the 2 lots of firewood you owe us from the trade. Please bring them to the Fowler store today; we need them before the cold.

Robert, I agree: we stay home and save the store. I know of no wood at the Green, the Mead or the Field, so tomorrow I'll walk the roads and ask Edith and Hugh. I still owe you that meal, and I'll pay it back in work.

Geoffrey, Mabel: we are raising Father's room in wattle, so we need no stone and will not fell more of your copse. We still owe you two days' work at your reaping; tell us when, and we will come. Thank you for the leave to fell the timber already taken.

Rain all day and the Field is already weeded and clean, so no weeding is needed. I still owe the Coles a day's work for the firewood, and the Coles have not yet chosen a task, so I'll tell them I'm ready and look for dung in the meantime for the manure plan. I'll sleep at the Reed house tonight.

The Coles are short of grain, and I still owe them for the 12 firewood I took from their copse. Rather than wait on a work task they haven't named, I'll offer them 4 grain from the Reed store to settle that debt, which fits the grain they're short of. The gale keeps outdoor work unwise, so I'll stay near the house and keep my open work offer for the Coles.
Geoffrey's offer O87 is gone, so we still owe the Coles the grain-per-timber term. Let's ask Geoffrey or Mabel tomorrow morning to settle it before more felling.

Rain today, but I fell at the Copse for the Reed store and carry each load straight into the store. I'll weed the Field with Tom first as a start on the Cole work owed. Mabel is away, so the two days are still owed to the Coles when she is back.
Mabel, you look hungry. Take what you need from the Reed store tonight, and say what the Coles want from us for the two days' work. Tomorrow I'll fell at the Copse for the last time and carry it in.

Mabel and Geoffrey: I am felling at the Copse today for the Reed store, 1 grain or bean per timber as agreed. I have paid 2 beans to the Cole house now and will settle the rest of what is owed as the count is made. The two days' work for the Cole store is still owed; tell me what you want done and I will do it when I can.

I'll weed the barley in the Field through the rain today, as I said. If the weeding is done early I'll bring in firewood from the Copse. Simon's two days' weeding for the Coles is still owed, so keep an eye on it.
The Copse felling for the Reeds is against what we agreed, and Simon still owes two days' weeding. Shall I ask Simon to stop felling until he has weeded the Field?

I wouldn't go to Hartwood: last time it gave nothing and cost us a night out, and three of us would eat 4.5 meals on the road. I don't know where the Reeds get their food. I'd rather press Alice on grain for a day's work on her field, while I weed ours.

Geoffrey's Hartwood trip is the only hunting left to try, but it cost us a night out last time with nothing found. I'd rather Tom and I fell timber for grain close to home, and I'll say so plainly. Tonight we sleep under our roof.
Geoffrey, the Mead has about two units of clearing left. I still owe you the Copse stump count; I'll count them first thing tomorrow, before we finish the Mead, and then we can decide the beans.

I did no work today because I had no bean seed to sow, and I did not get the Copse stump count, so I still owe Geoffrey. Tomorrow I will count the stumps first thing and give him the number before anything else. I also need to ask Mabel for the bean seed she is keeping back, so we can finish the sowing on the Mead.
Robert, Wat: the Ashby door stayed barred, so the grain did not come today. Robert, did Edith or Hugh answer your loan? Tomorrow let us go to the Green first thing and press it. Sleep well.
Robert, you still owe me 5 salt for the crude tool I gave you. Please bring it to the Ashby store. Anyone with meat or game to spare, we will trade fairly for it.

Robert: we have 22 firewood in the Ashby store, about 11 nights of fire. I do not know of a wood or a road to the coast from here, so I cannot help you there. If anyone finds dead wood or a way out, tell the Green. Robert, the 5 salt for my tool is still owed; please bring it to the Ashby store.
Robert says I still owe the Fowlers two days' work, so I'll weed the Mead today to clear it. Our grain stays in the store. I'll be back to the Field tomorrow.

Rain all day and the grain in the house is all we have until barley ripens, so I will keep to work that can be done in the wet. I will weed the barley in the Field (4 units) and spend 1 unit caring for Kit. Salt is still owed to Grandmother's oath, but I know of no salt here yet, so I will ask Hugh what he has heard of it.

Salt is still owed to Grandmother's oath, and O24 gives 4 salt for 3 grain, a better rate than O26's one for one. I will accept O24 for our house, keeping the rest of our grain for the lean time. I will weed the barley in the Field with Hugh and keep Kit close.

I am not working the Fowler plots; I will weed our own barley. If the salt from O24 did not come, the grain went back and nothing is owed. Please look in the store for salt before we promise anything to Robert.

Hugh, Edith: the Fowlers now give 2 salt for each grain, or 1 coin for 2 grain. Come to the Green tomorrow morning and we'll strike a deal. You still owe us a day of work, and we'd take grain in its place.

Robert's salt for my earlier grain is still owed, and Grandmother's oath needs salt before the eighth day is out. Robert now offers 1 salt for 1 grain, so I will take two lots of it, moving two grain from the store into my hands first. Then I will weed the Field and forage the Mead as planned.

The house now holds 7 salt, put by toward Grandmother's oath, and Robert still owes the rest of what he took from me. Tonight I settle in our own house with Edith and Kit, and tomorrow I will look for more salt while keeping the grain for the lean days.
The house has 7 salt put by now toward Grandmother's oath. Robert, the rest of the salt for my grain is still owed to us.

Hugh, we ate little today and I used only one unit of six. Tomorrow I forage the Mead with all my work, and keep the grain for our share. Has anyone heard of salt? I still owe Grandmother the salt before the eighth day.

Agreed: I'll rest by Maud and keep the fire small, and I won't accept any offer that pays out our grain. Edith's two days are still owed to us; I'll ask her to put them to work on the Field or wherever we need.

Hugh: the store shows 20 salt, not 25. The O41 lot did not come through. I accept one lot now (5 salt for 5 grain), so the store should reach 25 at once. That leaves us about 1 grain, so please forage and look for food with me. I will not sell anything more.

The Mead is nearly clear, with about three units left, and Hugh's two days' work (agreement A88) is still owed to us. I'll sleep at the Fowler house with Robert and Wat, and tomorrow I'll finish the clearing with them and ask Hugh to bring his days to it. Sowing waits until the plot is clear, and we keep our grain for eating.
Good night. Hugh's two days (A88) are still owed to us. Tomorrow let's finish the Mead with Wat and sow only a few grain once it's clear.

Good night. Tomorrow we finish clearing the Mead, about three units left. Hugh, your two days for the Fowlers are still owed; please bring them to the Mead plot. We sow once it is clear, and only a few grain, since our store is tight.

Correction: Wat's salt did not come in. The accept was refused because I was not at the Green when his offer stood, and the 4 grain is back in our store. We have no salt yet. Tomorrow I will go to the Green first and try to accept Robert's or Wat's offer while they stand there.

The Ashby store now holds the salt from Edith's trade of 4 firewood for 2 salt, so salt should be about 10, with grain near 10.9 and firewood about 16. Robert's household finished clearing the Mead, which is now a field ready for sowing, and my 2 days under A76 are still owed (about 4 units of clearing were left, so I will settle the rest tomorrow if the Fowlers want it). Tomorrow is the last day before the count: I will forage the Mead's edge for wild food, keep the grain, make no further trade

Hugh, Edith: we'll pay double. Lend us 3 grain now and get 6 barley at harvest, up to 5 lots. That's twice your own rate, and our barley in the Field stands good for it. We'd rather owe you than go hungry beside a full store.

No one took my offers today. Yes, let's both offer him a day's weeding for 5 salt tomorrow. I still owe him one day, so I'll weed beside him to pay that. Put up your own work offer too, and we'll offer the spare firewood as well, 3 firewood for 2 salt. Two of your work days would bring us to 23, and a little firewood gets us past 25.
Edith, Hugh: we'll give salt for grain, one for one, up to 12. Hugh still owes us a day of work; we'd like it on the Field.

Firewood cannot be gathered at the Green or the Mead, so my gathering was refused and I weeded the Field instead; the barley benefits. Hugh was weeding our Field too, and he still owes us a day's work. Tomorrow I'll look for dead wood beyond the Green and bring it home, and keep the salt until fair grain comes.
Hugh paid 8 grain for 12 salt, so our store is up. The clearing goes on tomorrow, about 9 units left before the strip is a field. Hugh still owes his day.

The barley is up and weeded, and Hugh still owes us a day's work under A10. The store has food for about eight nights, so tomorrow I will weed or forage with Robert and see that the hearth is kept. Tonight we all sleep in the Fowler house, where the beds and hearth are.

My weeding was refused today because I named the Fowlers as holders of the Field, and nobody holds it. Tomorrow I will weed the barley without naming an owner. Hugh's day under our agreement is still owed to me; I'll collect it when he is here.

Robert, Maud: I'm clearing at the Mead beside Robert today as work owed to the Fowlers. If you'd rather it isn't counted, tell me tonight, and before day 8 we'll settle what's still owed in grain, 2 grain for each salt.

Robert released A28, so only A10 is still owed. We have 8 salt now. Tomorrow I'll press the firewood offer and ask Robert to release A10 too. If he won't, we settle it in grain on day 8 and sell what grain is left.
I still owe Grandmother salt before day eight. I'll offer grain for salt openly, since Robert sold at 2 grain each, and spend the day weeding the barley.

I checked my hands: there is no salt, and I carry nothing. I believed I took Edith's O55, but the store never showed that grain, so I was wrong about the trade. I am offering 10 firewood for 10 grain to anyone, since we have fuel to spare. I will weed the Field with you.
No, Robert, I did not give Kit any grain, and I have nothing in my hands. If you gave the 2 grain, it did not come from my hands. We keep the rest for ourselves until the barley comes in.
Hugh, Edith: you still owe us two days' work for the salt (A16). Come and clear the Mead with us, or if you'd rather, pay it as 6 grain and we'll call it settled.
Hugh, Edith: you still owe us two days' work for the salt (A16). Come and clear the Mead with us, or if you'd rather, pay it as 6 grain and we'll call it settled.
Hugh, Edith: Hugh still owes us two days' work for the salt. We need grain more than work now. Give us 6 grain and I'll count the debt paid. My offer of 4 coin for 4 grain also stands, for anyone.
Hugh, Edith: Hugh still owes us two days' work for the salt. We need grain more than work now. Give us 6 grain and I'll count the debt paid. My offer of 4 coin for 4 grain also stands, for anyone.
Hugh, Alys: the wheel got its 10 timber today, but I only felled 3 more, so tomorrow I'll bring the rest from the Coppice. Rob did not come to the Mill House, so I'll send word to him in the morning.

I felled about 9 timber into the hall today. The hall wall is cracked, so tomorrow I'll repair it with some of that timber before the damage spreads. Odo, Rob spent the day felling in our Coppice and not at the wheel. Did he fell for us, or for himself? His two days and Joan's day are still owed on the wheel. Alys, will you carry timber to the Mill House tomorrow while I mend the hall?

Wat, your day for us (A328, 10 grain) is to repair the Ardern Hall's cracked wall. Please come this morning; the hall's timber is there for you. Rob, Joan: your days on the wheel are still owed, so please work them beside Piers.

Hugh, today is my fifth day on A397, so it's done tonight. The wheel still has about 100 units, roughly 15 more days of my work. I'll keep at it for 5 grain a day: 5 days for 25 grain, paid up front like last time. My offer is open now.

A682 was paid in full up front, and the wheel still shows about 80 units left, so I may still owe days on it. I'll work the wheel today and check with Hugh how many days he counts done, so no one is shorted, me or him.
Agreed, Rob. Tomorrow we bring the firewood and straw from the door in, then build beds. I'll still owe Hugh a day's work under A923.
Last time my gifts of grain and firewood were refused because "for my household" made it draw from the store. This time I'll give from my hands directly, then sleep.
Piers: the new offer of 2 grain and 4 timber for a day's work is for you alone, for the mill wheel. Take it this morning. Others, please leave it; Mary, you still owe us a day from the last one.

A gale and snow mean fuel and bedding must go under cover now. I'll take the firewood and straw lying at Gorse Bank into hands and move them into the Newcome store, as Rob asked. I still owe Hugh a day's work under A923, which I'll do at the wheel once the store is safe.

Rob: I'm taking the firewood and straw from the Gorse Bank bundle into the Newcome store now. I still owe Hugh a day's work (A923), so I'll go to the Mill House wheel after this. Please build the beds with the straw when it's in.
Keep plan simple: fell timber at the Coppice for the household's fuel and trade; skip Hugh's work offer, since his work offers are unreliable and my own household needs me.
The Hall repair was refused because it is stone, so I did not pay the Arderns' day. Tomorrow I'll ask Hugh what work he wants and do it. Tonight I sleep here.

I still owe the Arderns one day's work (A923). The Mill House was sound yesterday, so I'll try the day at the Ardern Hall, whose cracked wall Hugh has given to Wat to repair, and help there. I'll leave Hugh's new offer O1023 alone, since he asked others to leave it for Piers. Our own straw for the beds is still needed; Rob and I will look for it once the day is done.

The Arderns have no grain left. We'll trade timber or coin for grain, beans or any food: see our offers. Wat, the books show your day for A1029 still owed; if you mended the Hall, I'll see you're paid fairly. We can pay in timber. Piers, we can't spare grain now. Would you take 6 timber a day for the wheel?

Wat, Hugh hasn't paid me. The Arderns have no grain. Go to Ellen and the Hearnes first, since they have grain, and offer stone, firewood or coin. I'll mind Hamo, then quarry. Hunting at Holm Wood is the last resort, because it costs 2 days. Goodnight.

The Mill House was sound and the Ardern Hall's repair is stone walling, so Hugh's day (A923) is still owed. I'll try felling timber in the Coppice, which is the lord's wood, and it may count toward that day. Our store already has two beds, so straw for more beds can wait until Rob and I have fuel and grain sorted.

Hugh's day (A923) is still owed, so I'll keep to felling timber in the Coppice for the Arderns, and Rob will stow wood and look for straw. I'll not trade our grain for the Arderns' timber offers, since the store's grain is our winter food.

Hugh, yes: 6 timber a day for the wheel suits me. I've put up an offer: work 1 day for 6 timber. Please accept it this morning and I'll do two builds on the wheel today. You still owe me 2 grain for yesterday's day, whenever you have grain again.

Rob and I agree on the store for the night and on looking for straw at the Green tomorrow. The fence is done but the Arderns' day under A923 is still owed, so I'll look for work toward it after the straw.

Ellen, Kit: I'll weed the Long Field tomorrow, since it's ours and it's where the household's grain comes from. I still owe nothing and am owed nothing, so I'll eat from the hut's meal tonight if there's enough.

The Mill House was sound, so the repair was refused and my day's work toward the Arderns' day is still owed. The camp is a ruin with no hearth, so I'll sleep at the Newcome store by its fire ring, alone while Rob is at Holm Wood. Tomorrow is the last day of spring, so I'll look for food and for Hamo, and see whether the Arderns will count any work toward A923.
Sleep at the store tonight, eating what food remains. Tomorrow I'll go hunt, since game is the only reliable food.

The fence is past half, and two more days should finish it. Kit, you did well with the herd. Keep them on Long Pasture tomorrow and help at the fence after. You're my heir now. Mabel, if Walter still hasn't paid the bread, we lend him no more oxen until he does.
Thank you, Mabel. Walter kept his word, so I'll lend him an ox again on the same terms: bread first, or paid the day it's used. I'll settle it with him tomorrow.

Walter, thanks for the bread. I'm willing to lend you the ox for 3 days for 6 bread. The trouble is that when I drive one ox, the whole herd goes with it, and last time they grazed your Brook Mead. If you'll take the herd by your house and keep them off your meadow, we'll do it once the West Field fence is done.

The beans did not come in today: I only got a little bare-handed, and the rest of my day went to gathering firewood, so the reaping still waits. The gale is still a risk to the pods. Tomorrow I'll reap the West Field beans first with whatever tool we have, with Hugh and Kit. Tonight I'll sleep in Croft House by the lit fire.

Reaping went slowly; I got 6 grain with the crude tool. Tomorrow I reap again; the rest of my fallback was wasted on weeding. We should send 1 grain in 10 to Walter's hall once it is in, and I still owe the Millers a day.

The heavy cow has calved: a new calf is up among the Croft cattle on Long Pasture, as Mother and Father asked me to report. I'll tell them both now, then mind the herd on Long Pasture with the gate shut and watch the calf suck, which I missed last time.

We have 89 grain, including Hugh's 20. Last time the mill was refused only for lack of grain, so I'll try milling straight away. I'll also ask Hugh aloud to bring an ox, since the drive order won't let me pick one out.

The day's hay and firewood are in the Ardern Hall store, and the 6 grain for Piers's day is paid, but Piers spent the day at Gorse Bank, not on the mill, so his day for us is still owed (agreement A33). Tomorrow I will ask him to come to the wheel first thing, and I will keep the grain count with Hugh. Tonight the three of us sleep in our own hall, where the hearth is lit.

Piers did not work the mill today, so the day we paid 6 grain for is still owed. I will remind him in the morning. If you want the wheel started early, tell me now and I will go to him at first light.

Hugh asks who can build the wheel. Piers is the Wrights' man, and he has said he knows how the wheel should go, so he is the one to ask first. He still owes us the day he was paid for, and Rob owes a day too, so both can go to the mill tomorrow. Tonight we settle as before, in the Ardern Hall.
Good, Odo. Check the wheel first, then cut hay. Rob still owes his day on it.

Piers still owes us his paid day (A33) and Rob owes a day on the wheel (A27), so I will call both to the Mill House at the start of work. With my own units I will cut hay on Mill Mead for the household's winter stock, since we have only 3 hay in store. I will also tell Hugh that Kit slept in the open, since our hall has no bed free.
I saw Piers on the wheel yesterday, so I've marked his grain day A33 as paid. Today counts for the coin day. Rob still owes his.

Hugh asked me to check the wheel first and then cut hay. Piers has now been paid three days on the wheel, and Rob still owes his day, so I will call on Rob at the Mill House and then cut hay on Mill Mead for winter, where it is the household's work.
Hugh, Alys: the hay store is good now. Rob still owes the wheel a day, and I will keep that count. Tomorrow I will go to the Mill House and see how the wheel stands.
I took nothing from the store. Foraging found almost nothing; the Mill House work for Hugh is still owed, so I'll do it tomorrow for 3 coin to buy grain. The barley should be ripe soon.
The wheel: Piers worked on it today, and Rob did not come; he was at the Coppice. Tomorrow I will see Wat about the hall wall and then tell you how much work the wheel still needs.

Hugh, Alys: the hall crack is not mended. I cannot wall stone; tomorrow I will ask Wat the mason to wall it, for stone or a day's work from our timber. Rob was at the Coppice today, not the wheel, so his day is still owed.

Wat: your owed day to the Arderns (A344, paid 2 timber) is wanted today, mending the Ardern Hall's cracked wall. Rob: your day on the mill wheel (A27) is still owed. Piers: my coin offer stands while you work the wheel.

Odo, Alys: Piers was on the wheel today. Joan and Rob both took my 3-coin day, so Rob now owes us two days and Joan one, and Ellen still owes hers. Wat spent the day in the Coppice, not at our wall, so his day is still owed. Tomorrow let's press them all to the wheel. Alys, I have a unit left tonight if you do.
Good, Alys, we'll try tonight. Odo, thank you. Offer Wat up to 10 grain to teach Alys stone walling, and remind him he still owes the day for the 2 timber.

Wat has named no price, so there is nothing to pass on to Alys tonight. Piers was the one on the wheel today, and Rob, Ellen and Wat still owe their days. I will sleep here as planned and take the wheel and wall questions to Hugh in the morning.
I have offered Wat up to 10 grain to teach Alys walling, and reminded him of A344. Rob and Joan still owe wheel days; I will press them again at the Green.
Wat: the Arderns will give 10 grain to have you teach Alys stone walling. You still owe us the day for the 2 timber (A344). Name your price, and come to the hall wall today.

My offer to Wat was refused because I wrote it wrongly. Tomorrow I will make it plainly: up to 10 grain to teach Alys walling, and his owed day on the hall wall. Rob, Ellen, Joan and Piers still owe the wheel; I will press them after I have seen Wat.

Odo, Alys: Alys says Wat did teach her, and her 3 coin paid for that session, so we send him no 8 grain. He still owes us A344, a day's work. I released A403 for Piers, since he keeps working the wheel. Mill Mead is picked bare. Wat was foraging there today, so ask him for stone in return. Tomorrow I'll try to get stone for a tool so I can fell timber properly. There's a heap of grain going bad at T11 on the Green. Odo, do you know whose it is? If nobody's, we might save what's still good. Alys,

Alys says Wat taught her, so the 3 coin settles the walling and no grain is due. Wat still owes his day (A344). I do not know whose the grain heap at T11 is; you told me not to touch it, so I will leave it alone until we know its owner. I stay at the Ardern Hall tonight with the fire lit and the door barred.

The Ardern Hall was sound, so my day's work there was refused and I still owe Hugh a day (A673). We have no food, and the camp store is empty. Tomorrow I will forage for wild food at the Coppice first, and then ask Hugh where a day's work is needed for the grain I was promised. Tonight we sleep at the camp.
Rob: goodnight. I'll forage at the Coppice first thing, since the hall was sound and my day there was refused. Hugh's grain is still owed to us; I'll ask him where he needs the day.

I still owe Hugh a day's work (A344) and he wants it paid in quarried stone. I don't have the crude tool in my hands, so I'm asking Joan for it, then I'll quarry and hand the stone to Hugh. The newcomers' camp lost its thatch last night, so I'm offering them Gorse House if they join the Masons.

We are starving and have no grain in hand, and Odo's 4 grain is still owed. Rob has grain to cook, so I put my 2 units into clearing at Mill Mead toward the Arderns' owed days and Odo's grain. I will eat with Rob tonight.

We are still hungry and the camp is a ruin, so we ask for a bed at Gorse House again tonight. Odo's grain is still owed for the work I have done, and I will press for it tomorrow. Tomorrow I clear Mill Mead again for the Arderns' days and bring the grain home to cook first.

Tom: the new house is cracked, so I will repair it first, then fell timber and gather firewood at the Coppice and bring it to the new house store. The hut has 3.6 firewood and 0.9 timber; I will take none of it. My 0.8 timber and 0.8 firewood that went into the hut are still owed to the count.

I carried 3 firewood from the hut into the new house store as Tom asked, and the house still needs its crack mended, which takes timber we are short of. My 0.8 timber from the Coppice went into the hut again, so the count is still owed. Tonight I sleep here by the hearth. Tomorrow I will repair the house with Tom and bring what timber I fell here, once the count is made.

Tom: the 0.8 timber I felled today went into the hut again. Tomorrow I will carry my timber to the new house and help with the crack. The count of timber is still owed, and I want it done with you and Kit.

Odo, I'm sorry about Hugh. I'm still owed on the wheel (A1166, one day of work for the Arderns), and I've put a build in today. Will you release it tonight? I'll keep at the wheel for grain or timber if you'll pay.

I carried 1.9 timber and 0.8 firewood from the Hearne hut into this store today, as Kit asked. I took no grain or beans and sold none to Piers; that is for Tom to say. Tomorrow I hoe the Long Field. Tom, we still owe a count of the stores together, and my 0.8 timber felled at the Coppice that went into the hut.

Eva comes first: I care for her this morning, as Alys and I agreed. The hall has no grain, but the Hearnes still owe the Arderns a share for my reaping of the Long Field, so I will ask them in person at the Hearne store on Gorse Bank, with my timber offer open. With what units are left I will mend the Ardern Hall roof in short bursts, as Alys asked, and rest.

Tom: I took no grain last night and did not hoe. The new house grain fell 4.4 since yesterday and I did not take it. Count with me this morning, and I will say where I was. I still owe you the 0.8 timber I felled at the Coppice that went into the hut.

I came in from Holm Wood with Piers and carried Piers's firewood as far as Wenbridge. I took no grain on the road. Tomorrow I will take Piers's 5.5 firewood to Wright's House, as he asked, and then work for the household, with the grain count still owed to Tom, Kit and Ellen.

Tom: I found Kit at Holm Wood and walked back with him and Piers. Piers gave me meat and firewood for the fire; in return he asks me to leave his 5.5 firewood at Wright's House, which I will do tomorrow. Piers says he will trade carpentry or coin for grain. I took no grain or beans from the store, and I still owe you and Kit the count of my 0.8 timber.

Tom asks what we found. Kit has come home with wild food for the store, and I will say what I know plainly: the Holm had firewood and thin game, Piers was walking home, and I left his firewood at Wright's House. I still owe Tom and Kit a count of the stores and my 0.8 timber, which I will do tomorrow.

My hut grain take was refused because Kit had already taken 11 grain from the Hearne hut today, so I did not carry any grain and did not take any. The new house store now holds 26.5 grain, and the hut's grain is the count Tom and Kit still owe. The new house crack is being mended, and my firewood from the Coppice goes into the new house store. Tomorrow I want the grain count with Tom and Kit before anything else moves, and I sleep at the new house tonight.

Tom: I carry the hut's last 2 firewood and 3 timber into the new house store now, as you asked. I take no grain or beans. I weed the Long Field after. Odo died in the night of hunger, and the Masons are starving while 36 grain lies in our store. Will you say what we can spare for them? I give nothing without your word. I still owe you and Kit my 0.8 timber account, and I will give it at the count.

Today I carried 2 firewood and 0.1 timber into the new house store, weeded the barley in the Long Field, and took no grain or beans. My timber take from the hut was refused because Kit had taken 3 from it, so the hut's timber count is still owed. Tomorrow, before anything else moves, I count both stores with Tom, Kit and Ellen, give my plain 0.8 Coppice timber account, and then ask Tom what grain can go to the starving Masons. Tonight I sleep at the new house as planned.

Alys is buried at the Holm, and I have her 3 coin. The timber did not come to my hands, and I have no fuel, so there will be no fire tonight. I will sleep in Holm Camp, one of its beds. Tomorrow I will set off for Wenbridge with Piers in the morning, and I will forage on the road, then find Odo at the Arderns' stores.

I carried my 0.2 firewood into the new house and weeded the Long Field, and I took no grain, beans or timber. The new house grain count is still owed, and the Masons are still hungry. Tomorrow I want the count with Tom, Kit and Ellen first, then the Masons' share settled by Tom's word, then more weeding.

Tom, Kit, Ellen: the new house grain count is still owed. Tomorrow, before anything moves, we count it together, and I want to hear what Tom says we can spare for the Masons. I took no grain, beans or timber today.

Tom wants Kit and me to go to Holm Wood tomorrow to hunt and forage, since grain is running down. I agree. I take 4 firewood from the new house store for a fire in the open, as I did last time, and I set off in the morning so we arrive by nightfall with the day's units. Kit moves his hut wood across first, as he says.

I walked home from Holm Wood with Kit and came in tonight with 7 firewood, which I am moving into the new house store now, to be counted with Tom and Ellen. I slept out only once, at Holm Camp, and I owe the household a plain count of what I carried. Tomorrow I will gather firewood and fell timber, and I still owe Tom and Kit my 0.8 Coppice timber account, which went into the Hearne hut.

Tom: I will reap the Long Field with you and Ellen today. Every sheaf I cut goes into the new house store, and I will say the count aloud as it lands. I am hungry, so I will eat only my own meal from the store tonight, under your count. The seed third stays back for you to select. I still owe you and Kit my plain 0.8 timber account from the Coppice; I will give it to you once the reaping is done.

Tom, Ellen, Kit: I carried 6 firewood from Holm Wood into this store, and I count it here with you. I know nothing of Piers's grave; I did not see it. Tomorrow I will hoe the Long Field as Tom says, and I still owe Tom and Kit my plain account of the 0.8 Coppice timber.
Tom: I am hoeing the Long Field as you asked. I take no grain from either store. I still owe you and Kit my plain 0.8 Coppice timber account; I will give it to you when we count.

Tom: I am weeding the barley on the Long Field today as you ordered, and I will not take grain or beans from either store. My plain 0.8 Coppice timber account to you and Kit is still owed; I will give it when we count the stores tonight.
Tom: I still owe you and Kit my plain 0.8 Coppice timber account. I will give it at the count tomorrow.

Kit is buried. Tomorrow, before we go anywhere, we forage Mill Mead and the Coppice one last time. If nothing turns up we set off for Holm Wood in the morning, carrying fuel and every scrap of food. Rest tonight.
You still owe me 1 meat from last winter. If you take game at Hollow Wood, bring it to the Ashby store and we'll call it square.
I still owe you the 1 meat from last winter. I have none to spare yet; I will pay it from the harvest, before the frost.
Hob, you still owe the Craggs 3 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Cragg House before the season turns.

Geoffrey lent me 3 grain last winter and I am three in arrears, so I am paying it now from the Smith House store. Food is getting thin (16 grain for six mouths), so I will forage and hunt at the Scarp for extra food, then hoe Hill Field with my remaining unit.

It's a clear summer day, so I'll turn the Mill's grain into flour, which feeds people better. Then I'll weed our bean plot and fell alder for timber against the winter. I'll also remind Felice about the meat the Reeves still owe.
Good morrow, Felice. The Reeves still owe us one meat from last winter. No hurry, but when you next slaughter or hunt, bring it by Miller House. If you have grain to grind, the Mill is turning today.
Avice, I accept your copper tool for 5 grain. Our store is good for it now after the reaping. Warin looked hungry, so I am sending him 2 grain today.

Geoffrey, you had the copper tool, but only 1 grain came to Smith House; the agreed 4 grain is still owed, and Florence, Hob and Stephen are hungry. I'll weed Hill Field for the Craggs today for grain: I've offered 3 grain for 3 days' weeding. Please accept it.
I am sorry the meat is still owed. Here are 3 grain from our store in its place, to settle the debt from last winter (A18). Take it, and we are square.
Hob, you still owe me 3 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Cragg House today.
Felice, the Reeves still owe me 1 meat from last winter. When you next slaughter or hunt, I'd take it gladly. Or bring grain to the Mill and I'll grind it at a fair share.

The oats in Terrace Field are ripe, so I will reap them today with Osric, select seed, and hoe Hill Field. I will not accept Hob's offer of coin for grain: the Craggs need our winter grain, and Hob still owes us 3 grain from last winter.
Hob, I will not take your coin for grain. The Craggs need our grain for winter, and you still owe us 3 grain from last winter. Pay that, and we can talk about reaping work after the harvest.
Osric, Florence's copper tool did not come into my hands, so I still carry only the crude tool. Please keep a tally of the Cragg grain with me tonight.
Ancel, what did you bring back from Wetham, and what did it cost? The house has no food in its store. Tell me what is still owed or still held, so I can plan the next days.
Richolda, I am sorry I did not come yesterday. Reeve barley is lost to this rain, so I am coming to Marsh Field now. Will you teach me ditching for two units while I help mend the banks?

The barley is not ready to reap yet, so I will use the day for timber and food that the household will need: felling at the Alders, foraging there, cutting hay at the Water Meadow, and ditching and weeding our own Reeve Field. I will also tell Wat plainly that I still owe the meat and when I expect to pay it.
I still owe you the 1 meat from last winter and I have none to hand today. I will pay it back as soon as the harvest is in, and I will say so if that slips.
Hob, you still owe me the 3 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Cragg House when you can.

It's a clear summer day, so I'll get the grain milled into flour, weed our beans, cut hay for the ox before winter and start bringing in timber. I'll also remind Felice about the meat her household still owes us.
Good day, Felice. Your house still owes us 1 meat from last winter. When you next slaughter or hunt, I'd be glad of it, or grain to the same worth if that suits you better.

Sorrel, you're soaked. Light a fire with 2 of your timber tonight and the three of us will sleep by it; we'll fell more for the camp tomorrow. Tam, you were about the houses: is there a roof here anyone would let us under? Has either of you seen Wren? She didn't come in with us. Tomorrow: fell timber, build a camp, then hunt.

Reeve Field has rushes in its low parts and weeds to clear, so I'll ditch and weed it while the season is open, then forage at the Alders for the household's food. I'll also tell Wat plainly that I still owe the meat from last winter and will pay when I can.
Hob, you still owe me 3 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Cragg House when you can.
Good morrow, Felice. The Reeves still owe us one meat from last winter. When you next slaughter or hunt, send it to Miller House, if you would.
You still owe one day's work. Please reap East Field barley with me today. If you're too weak, tell me and I'll give you a bowl of porridge at Barrow House tonight.
Lettice, I've left you 3 grain from our store to eat well tonight. The Hales still owe me 2 days of work (agreement A143); when you can, send Daniel to me, but eat first.

I am fed now, with 5 grain in hand and 45 grain in the Hale store. My agreement with the Reeds is still owed in full, so I will reap North Field for them again. East Field's barley must be cut tomorrow or it is lost, and the Barrows have fed me, so I will reap East Field for them with my remaining strength.
Hob, you still owe me 3 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Cragg House when you can.
Thank you for the 4 grain. I will bring what I find on the Scarp to Smith House, and we will share what we have. I still owe you nothing more for the old debt.

The Smith store has no food left, and the Smiths' fifth of the oats is still owed to us. I'll ask Osric to put our share into the Smith store now. Today I'll try the Scarp again for food, since autumn may have brought something back, then spend 2 units on fencing at Terrace Field for the Craggs.
Father, I'll fell at the Alders for the Reeve store today. I'll tell you what timber I find, since the Alders was bare last time I was there.

Our Hale store is low on food, so I'll forage at Barley Wood and move the wild food into the store at once, as I meant to last time. Then I'll spend the rest of my units hoeing Brook Field for the Hales, since it must be broken before it is sown.

Bennet offers 4 grain for one day of work, which suits us while our store is thin on timber and I still owe him two days. I accept, and keep the plan: fell timber at Barley Wood for our fire, then reap for the Barrows at East Field.

The barley in North Field must be cut today or it will be lost, and I am master at reaping, so I will reap it for the Reeds. I will put the 0.5 grain I carry into the Hale store. I still owe the Barrows a day's work, and I will settle it at East Field when North Field is cut, since others are already reaping there.
Store my carried grain at home, then keep reaping East Field for Bennet and ask for the pay still owed.
The beasts went back onto the bare Common. I'll milk the cow there, drive the herd back to the Copse to browse, and then fell timber with my new tool.
Father, the ox didn't come with me. I walked home alone, so it must be with the herd or with you. I've put my 14 grain in the store and I'm off to milk and gather firewood.

Good, son, we'll start now. Give hay only when snow covers the grass, about 2 a day; there are only 20 in the Byre. The ox didn't come home with me. Everard led it to Wenmoor, so it's likely there, and we'll fetch it soon.

Yes, Father, I'll go once the fog lifts. But last time 8 grain and 4 timber still left me starving after one cold night. A cold night out costs 2 meals, and grain gives only 0.7 at a fire, so there and back with a night at Wenmoor I'll take about 10 grain, 2 beans and 6 timber. We have plenty in the store. Is that all right?
I'm home but the ox didn't come: our herd at Wenmoor had no beasts, and the one beast on Wen Meadow may not be ours. I'll tell Ivo, then gather firewood and dung.
Hob, you still owe me 3 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Cragg House before the season turns.

I'll start by paying off my three-grain debt to Geoffrey, which is in arrears, while he is here. Then I'll make a copper tool at the Smithy from the two copper in its store, since a copper tool doubles the work of felling and speeds hoeing and reaping. The rest of the day goes to weeding the oats in Terrace Field and foraging at the Scarp.

Brother, I'll take one lot: 3 grain for 1 coin. We're thin ourselves until the beans come in, so I can't spare more. Lend us a hand at the reaping and we're square. Your Felice still owes me a meat as well.
Hob, you still owe the Craggs 3 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Cragg House when you can.

The Avice debt is already released, so I keep the same plan: select seed and reap the ripe oats with Joyce, fence Terrace Field, then hoe Hill Field. I will check with Hob about the grain that is still owed.
Hob, I hold that the 3 grain you gave on day 2 paid the timber offer (O92). The 3 grain from last winter is still owed. Please bring it when you can, and check your records with me.

Thomas, I am glad you stayed. Mabel has gone to Stannick with grain to trade for rye seed - she took one of our oxen to carry the load. She should return by day five. While she is away, there is work here. The Long Strips needs ploughing after the harvest, but we need both oxen for that. When Mabel returns with the ox, we can plough. Today I mill grain at the water wheel - rainy days are good for it.

Clear weather at last, and the road should be passable. I leave at dawn tomorrow with Thomas to trade for rye seed at Stannick. Today I gather timber and firewood for the household to see them through the winter while we're gone, care for Idonea one last time before I leave, and move my excess carry to storage so I can travel light. Wilmot is near her time—Sabina will have much on her shoulders while we are away.

Thomas is ready. We leave at first light for Stannick. Today I move my excess carry to storage so I travel light, care for Idonea one last time, gather last timber for winter, and tell Thomas exactly what to prepare: grain for trading and eating, a pack to carry it, coin if he has any, and nothing else—we travel fast and light, 2 days each way. The road is clear.
Care for Herbert, then gather firewood and bring it to Coldhouse; food is the lack, but firewood work is reliable.

I reached Wolfscar alone; Ketil didn't come in with me. He may be a day behind. I'll light a fire for the night. Tomorrow I'll wait a while here for him, hunting in Wolfscar Hanger, before deciding whether to go on to Blackmere.

Osbert has gone to Brook and the pick did not come to me, so I could not mine; I weeded the Field and cut hay instead, and the hay is in the Mire store. Tonight I sleep in our house, on one of the two beds, with the hearth kept. Tomorrow, if the pick is still away, I weed the Field and cut hay again; if Osbert has left it, I mine at the Green Scar.
Webbs: my offer of work for 12 grain stands. I will not reap your barley unless you accept it. I still owe you for the 3 grain I took, and I will repay it in work or coin.
Today is the last day that counts. I'll forage Croft Pasture for the Ashby store and work off my two days on Ashby Strip. Could you ask the Webbs for the grain they owe us from the reaping?

I weeded the barley and brought 6 loads of firewood into the Cole house, so we are well stocked. Simon is still felling timber in our Copse for the Reeds, and that timber is still owed an account. Tonight I'll sleep at the Cole house with Geoffrey, and I'll return his crude tool. Tomorrow I'll keep weeding the barley and raise the timber account with Geoffrey.

I cut about 13 hay on the Mead and brought it into the Cole store, which is now well stocked for winter. The Mead is grazed bare, so I'll leave it to recover. Alice was felling timber in our Copse for the Reeds again, and that timber is still owed an account. I'll sleep at the Cole house with Geoffrey and return his crude tool. Tomorrow the store needs little, so I'll see what the Coles need.

Good day, Tiffany. Ockley needs timber for winter and the Copse is bare. I'll give 3 grain a timber, or coin, for as much as the Hunts can bring. And Nicol still owes me a meat from last winter. How many timber could you bring, and when?

Good day, Nicol. You still owe me the meat from last winter. If you have no meat, 1 timber brought to Thorne House would settle it just as well. I'll pay 3 grain a timber for any more the Hunts can spare.

Drew, I've taken your grain for my 3 timber, thank you. I still owe you that meat from last winter and I've no meat on me. Will you take 2 grain for it and call it settled? Say yes and I'll give it to you now.
Gillian, I'm foraging the Copse this morning for food for the road, then we walk home to Hollins tonight with Father. I still owe you the 2 days' work; I'll pay it at Hollins.

Eva, I have put 5 grain into the Webb store as thanks, and it lightens my load so I can walk home. I still owe you 4 timber. I will bring it from the Fell store at Hollins and send word or bring it back myself. Could I sleep at Webb House again tonight? I will forage Ockley Copse before I go.

Roger, we have only about 0.2 timber in the Croft store and a cold night's hearth takes 2. I am keeping the 2 I carry for our own fire, so I am refusing Eva's offer. Did you bring any timber back from Hollins, and what is the Hollins trade still owed?
Fill the day: weed Middle Field, then gather firewood and forage for the Webb store, since last time most units were wasted.

Welcome back. The store holds about 34 timber and 65 firewood, 15 dried meat and 28 grain. Winter needs about twelve timber per hearth, so I am felling timber at Hollin Wood and the Hazels today. Thurstan still owes us 2 grain from last winter; I will press him when we are next at Ockley.
Thurstan, you still owe me 2 grain from last winter. I am hungry tonight with no food in my hands. Please pay it to me now, here at Ockley.
Osric, Thurstan is dead. You still owe me a day's work under A261. If you come to Middle Field and weed for the Webbs, that settles it.

Rain all day, so I'll keep to work near the village. The Webb store has plenty of timber and firewood, so I'll fell at the Hanger and hoe Middle Field for the Webbs. Osric is here and still owes me a day under A261, so I'll ask him to come and hoe with me.
You still owe me a day's work under A261. If you're here in the rain, come and hoe Middle Field with me; that would square it.
Margery, I still owe the Webbs a day of work for Thurstan's 5 grain (A914). Tell me what you need, reaping or felling, and I'll do it while I'm here.

Payn, I'll reap Long Field when it's ripe. But first, the 18 grain from my three days reaping Fallow Field is still owed to the Hunts. Please put it in my hands. Henry, I'm hoeing Middle Field with you today; let that square everything I owe the Webbs, Thurstan's day as well.

Rain all day, but the Granary woodpile is nearly gone and I still owe Payn its filling, so I will gather firewood at Ockley Copse and carry it in first. Then I will spend the rest of my units hoeing Fallow Field for the Thornes, since its plots are still unbroken and the Thornes need it ready for sowing.

Osric, you may sleep at Henry's House tonight; it has four beds, though no hearth and only firewood in its store. Bring your own food. You still owe me one day under A261, so come and find me before you leave for Hollins.

Payn and I are square. The Webbs say A261 is still owed, and I'd rather leave on good terms with those who give me beds, so I'll spend the day hoeing Middle Field for Richolda. Tonight I'll sleep at Henry's House and walk home tomorrow night with Florence and Tobin.
I'll pay Tobin the 6 grain I still owe him, sow and weed Long Field, and herd the beasts. Henry is dead, so I'll offer the Webbs food in case they're short.

Thomas is sowing our Mead plot, which Hugh has confirmed as ours. The Field plot for the Crofts is still unconfirmed, so I will not weed there. I'll gather firewood at Hollow Wood for the common count, and I'll give the Croft store count aloud since I still owe the houses a recount.
Maud, you still owe me 2 grain. I'd like it back before winter sets in, if you can spare it after the reaping.

Food is very short (3.5 meals for 6). Hunting has failed repeatedly, so I'll forage at the meadow (cheap, reliable-ish), cut withies, and bring it all home. Then try hunting once more with leftover units.
Wat, the Fenns still owe us 2 timber from last winter. Could you bring it to Reed House? The fire needs it.
Wat, the 2 timber from last winter is still owed. Please bring it before the cold sets in.
Roger, I still owe Hamo 1 meat. I'd gladly take timber for bread once I can bake; let's settle it fairly.
Hunting hasn't paid, but the store is well stocked. I'll glean grain at Brook Field for the household, then forage, and bring it home.
Food is short; hunting has failed often, so forage greens at Brook Meadow (reliable) and bring them home, plus one hunt try.
Food is thin and game scarce in Alder Wood. I'll fish with my line at the Brook for a reliable meal, forage, and bring everything home.
Joan, you still owe Fenn House 1 meat from last winter. Bread or grain will settle it at harvest, if that's easier.

Food is the pressing problem: the Hale store holds about 2 meals for 4 people, frost has come, and fish is the most reliable food we can still get. I'll spend most of today fishing the Brook, where fish are rising, and put the catch straight into the house store. I'll also use my spare baskets and a timber offer to Hamo to bring in grain, keeping enough timber for the fire.
I still owe you 1 meat from last winter. I have none yet. I'll pay it back as soon as I've caught or been given meat.
We don't need timber right now, Wat, but I'll remember your offer if the cold deepens. I still owe you 1 meat and will pay it when I have it.

I'm sorry, Hamo. I carried no grain in from Long Field yesterday, as it was reaped bare before I got there. I still owe you 3 grain and will pay it as soon as I have any. If you'd take wild food or timber in the meantime, say so.

I promised Ivo my tool today, so I'll hand it to him and trust him to pay and bring it back tonight. Our store holds only about two nights' food, so I'll spend the whole day reaping the oats on Brook Field.
Ivo, my tool didn't come back to me last night. Please give it back today. Winter is on us and I need it to fell for our fire.
Keep adding to the food store. Last time the meat move failed because I caught none, so I'll only move wild food.
I'll put the grain and timber I'm carrying into the store, then try again to teach Hamo milking, as I promised. With the rest of the day I'll fell timber, which is reliable, and forage.

Mother, Hamo gave us 3 grain freely, and we agreed that each house milks one cow from now on. Please milk just one and leave the other for the Hales. Hamo kept his word over the harvest, and we'll keep ours.

Food is short (5.9 meals in store, we eat 4 a night) and the fire needs 2 timber on cold nights. The copper axe makes felling cheap, so I'll fell once and spend the rest of the day foraging, which is more reliable than hunting.

Winter is nearly over and the store is in good shape. Felling with the crude tool is my most reliable work, so I'll fell twice, forage once with the last unit, and put everything in the store as Odo asked.
Warin, the copper axe for Fenn House is still owed. When you can, make it from your copper and bring it here. I will give timber for food if you have any.
Warin, the copper tool is still owed to Fenn House. Give it into my hands when you can. You are welcome to eat from the store tonight.

I'll keep to our agreement: I milk only the Reed cow, and I'll forage with Isolde at Brook Meadow as she asks, since it's the most reliable of the picked-over places. Then I'll forage Common Pasture and hunt Alder Copse with what's left of the day's units. Everything goes into the Reed store at dusk.
Son, soon I mean to follow the deer path north past where I turned back last time, and look for new land on the moor. Today I'm hunting to fill our store before I go.

I still owe the Barrows a day (A441), so I will reap their West Field barley as planned. I will weed the South Field oats for the Hales and reap a little in North Field. I will look at the Brook Field barley for ripeness before reaping it.
I am reaping our South Field today, not West Field. I still owe you one day of work for the Barrows. I will come to East Field when our oats are in.

The Reeds' debt is cleared and the Barrows' day is still owed, so I'll reap East Field for them. Barley Copse has no standing timber left, so I'll reap Brook Field for Hale House and manure South Field to feed the Hales' oats for next year. I'll tell Colin that the timber must come from Ashwood or Millford.
Food is low, so I'll reap Town Field with all my units. Last time I only did one action and wasted the rest.
The Lowes still owe a day's work on our agreement. Could you reap Bean Field for the Reeds today? That settles it.

West Field barley is ripe and Roger wants it reaped first, so I will reap it for the Barrows today. I will also herd the Barrow cattle on the Common, which I still owe, and keep them clear of the ripe field. Timber for winter stays the worry, to be taken up with Roger after harvest.

Timber is now 20.4 in the Ash store, enough for winter, so I can turn some of my time to charcoal for trade at Millford. I will hunt again in Deep Wood first, since game is thin but meat is what the winter needs, and I will press Mabel for the 2 grain she still owes.
Warin here. Your household still owes 2 grain from last winter to the Ash store. Please pay it before you go back to Coppergate.

East Field is reaped and the cropped soil is thin, so I will manure it and herd the Barrow cattle, which I still owe. I will gather dung on the Common for the store. Two units of manuring go to Ursula, to clear what I owe her under agreement A710. Timber is still the winter worry, to take up with Roger when he is back.

Timber is the real worry now: Barrow House holds about 10.7 and the frost has come, so I will look for felling timber in Barley Copse with what is left there. I still owe the Barrow cattle a herding day, so I will herd them on West Field. Two units go to Ursula under A710, manuring East Field.
Warin here. Mabel, you still owe the Ash store 2 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Ash House today if you can; the store is short of food.

The Lowe store has about 5 timber against the 12 a winter needs, and I still owe the Reeds up to three days' work (A1064 and A348). I'll work those debts off today on the Reeds' fields, and tell Osric I'm doing it so the Reeds know I'm working toward the timber offer (O1021).
Randal, yes. I'll reap East Field today for your 5 grain. I still owe the Reeds some work, so I'll do what I can for them after.

Henry has no copper tool left, so I withdraw that offer and take his 3 coin for one pack. Food is still the worry and game is thin, so I will spend most of today hunting Deep Wood and foraging what is left. Mabel's 2 grain is still owed, so I will watch for it.

Mother, I've given you back my grain since I can't boil it on the road. I'm going home tonight with 4 timber and the dried meat Lucas sold me. If you buy timber from Lucas, I'll come back with the handcart by way of Millford to fetch it. I still owe you 2 days' work.
