Warin, I'm Matthew of Millford, hungry and with grain but no fire. Could you host me at Ash House tonight and let me boil my grain at your hearth? I'll give you 2 grain for it and still owe you the meat from last winter, which I'll repay.
Lucas, the 16 timber is for Miller House, to be fetched by Mariot, and it is not a full settlement. I still owe Alys for her care, and I have put 1.5 more in her store today. Thank you for asking.

The ox didn't come with me, so I can only carry about 7 timber. I'll trade 2 bread for 3 timber from Lucas and buy about 4 more with coin, then head home tonight while Ysolt fells with the copper tool.

Timber is the winter crisis: Barrow House holds about 2.6 timber and a cold hearth takes 2 a night, while food is secure with 176.8 grain in the house and 114.6 in the Granary. Today I'll herd the Barrow cattle on West Field, which I still owe, and spend the rest of my units on the West Field fence for the Barrows, and I'll hold Barrow timber for the hearth until Roger is back from Ashwood.

Hawise is taking bread and grain to Ashwood for timber, so I'll stay home, keep the Barrow hearth banked, and herd the Barrow cattle on West Field, which I still owe. Lettice is fencing West Field to pay me, so I'll fence beside her with my other units to finish it sooner.

Last winter day, and Smith House has only 1.8 timber against a cold hearth that burns 2 a night. Willow Holt has no standing timber, so I'm looking for timber through trade: Everard still owes me 3 timber for my 3 flour, and I'll offer flour to anyone who can spare timber, especially the Bells, whose woodpile is large. I'll also forage at Riverside Meadow with the rest of my work.
Everard, you still owe me 3 timber for the 3 flour I gave you. Smith House's fire is down to 1.8 timber. Please bring it to Smith House if you can.

Sabina still lies at the Clearing. I'm giving most of today to burying her. If you can spare a couple of units, join me and we can finish it. Please keep my bed at Ash House tonight. The cold nearly finished me last time.

The Barrow fire went out with only 0.8 timber left, and Hawise is at Ashwood buying more, so timber is still the crisis. Food is secure, so I'll herd the Barrow cattle on West Field, which I still owe, and fence the rest of West Field with Lettice, and I'll tell Roger what the timber position is so we decide the fire together.

I am hungry with nothing but 2 timber, and I still owe Lucas for his bed and table. I will offer him 1 timber for a loaf, keeping the other for the repair of Hale House, and forage and hunt at Deep Wood for wild food. Then I will sleep at Fenn House and walk home to Barleyfield once the rain eases.
Lucas, I am hungry. I offer you 1 timber for 1 bread now, and I still owe you work for the rest. May I sleep at Fenn House again tonight?
Ursula, I am home. I have put my 4 timber and my last grain into the Barrow store for the hearth. I still owe you 2 days' work under A710, and I will pay it as soon as the West Field fence is done.
Emma's two flour went to her when I accepted her offer, and the two days of work are still owed to me. I will keep hoeing Town Field and tell her so.

I am hungry and carry no food, and the grain offers were refused last time because Fenn has no store here. I will accept both offers into my own hands, so I can carry the grain home. Beatrix's strays are trampling her beans, so I herd them out of Bean Field and mend its fence. I forage at Brook Meadow for wild food to eat now, and I ask Beatrix to host me and feed me tonight.

Mariot, I am reaping Town Field for the Millers today, since the hoeing cannot be done while the barley stands. Could the Mill give me 2 grain for the reaping? I still owe you the two days' hoeing once the field is clear.

Henry is walking to Ashwood tonight, and I still owe Warin 2 grain from last winter, so I'll take 2 grain from the Moor store and give it to Henry to carry to Warin. I'll forage on High Pasture with my unit for the household.

This is the last day of the season and our timber is low (3.7 in store) against the twelve each hearth wants for winter, so I will fell timber in Deep Wood for the household, hunt there for game, and forage with any time left. I will also remind Matthew of the meat he still owes.
Matthew, you still owe me one meat from last winter. Bring it to Ash House when you can.
The ox didn't come with me, so I can only haul about 9 timber home on the handcart. I'm offering coin and grain for timber and for a night's lodging, and I'll do some felling myself.

Warin lent me 2 grain last winter and I still owe it, so I'll pay what I carry now. Timber is what the Forge and our hearth need, and I have a copper tool that doubles felling, so I'll fell timber in Deep Wood today. Henry stays to learn charcoal burning.
I know I still owe you one meat from last winter. I have none to hand yet, but I mean to pay it as soon as we have a beast slaughtered.
Hob, you still owe the Craggs 3 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Cragg House before the harvest.
Felice, the Reeves still owe me 1 meat from last winter. When you next slaughter or hunt, bring it to Miller House and we'll call it square.

Reaping is not ripe yet, and I have no tools, so I will weed our own barley at Reeve Field, which keeps the crop healthy, and forage at the Alders for wild food to ease the household's store. I will also tell Wat plainly that I still owe him the meat.

I owe Geoffrey 3 grain from last winter, and it is in arrears, so I will take 3 grain from our Smith House store and hand it to him. Then I will weed the growing oats in Terrace Field, hoe Hill Field, and fell timber at the Scarp to stock the store for the autumn sowing and the smithy fire.

Felice, the Reeves still owe me 1 meat from last winter. When you next slaughter, or if you have something else to give instead, I'd take it gladly. Bring your grain to the Mill too; I'll grind it for the usual share.
Osric still owes us 2 timber from last winter. When Osric is next at the Green, please collect it and put it in the Reed store.
Foraging is reliable and Deep Wood is rich in berries and nuts, so I'll forage all day to build the food store.
Food is still short, and Common Pasture is thick with berries and greens, so I'll forage there. I'll ask Cecily again to teach me milking, since she didn't come yesterday.
I'll forage in Deep Wood all day for reliable food.

Hamo is still owed his milking lesson, and it has to happen before the cows are milked. I will teach him at Common Pasture first thing (2 units), then milk the cows myself (1 unit), and use my last unit grinding grain into flour at Reed House for the household.

Milk the cows in milk at Common Pasture first, since I am the master at it and milk is needed fresh. Then use the rest of the day's units to fell timber and forage at Alder Copse, because the Reed store is low on timber for the fire and the Smiths still owe us wood. I will store what I bring in at Reed House.
Please press Osric of the Smiths for the 2 timber they owe us; it is in arrears. I am milking and felling today.

The Millbrook cattle have broken into Long Field and are trampling the barley, so I will first call everyone to drive them out. Then I will milk the cows in milk at Common Pasture, put the milk in the Reed store, and fell timber at Alder Copse, since the store's timber is needed for the hearth and the Smiths still owe us.
Osric of the Smiths still owes us 2 timber from last winter. When someone goes to Coppergate, please press him for it. I am milking at Common Pasture today and felling at Alder Copse for our store.

The Fenn store is nearly out of meat and holds about 24 meals for four or five eaters a night, so food is now the urgent problem. I will spend today's five units on foraging, which yields the most reliable food, with only one short hunt, and I will ask Simkin and the guests to forage too.
First I'll settle the 4 grain I still owe Hamo, handing it to him plainly with no "for" this time. Then I'll sow Long Field with the Hales, milk, and forage for the store.

I never set off last night, and I still owe Elena 8 wild food by day 7. I'll forage for the store today, top up what I carry to 9.5 wild food (8 for Elena and my meal on the road), and leave for Coppergate at nightfall to pay her and collect the copper tool from Warin.

We are starving and the store holds only about 3 meals for four mouths, so food comes first: I will forage the Hillside with my units for the household, then smelt some ore into copper we can trade for grain at Ashwood. I will also press Simkin for the 1.2 food still owed under A224 and any grain Fenn can spare.
Simkin, you still owe us 1.2 wild food under A224. Please bring it to the Smith store today. If Fenn has any grain or bread to spare, bring that too; we will pay copper for it.
The Reed fire now takes 2 timber a night and we hold about 8. I am felling what is left at Alder Copse, but we need timber from Ashwood or Coppergate soon, and Osric still owes us 2.
Osric, the Smiths still owe the Reeds 2 timber and it's in arrears. If you can't bring timber, 1 coin would square it. Which will it be?

I'm starving and carry only my copper tool, so I need food I can eat tonight. I'll spend my two units hunting in Deep Wood for food I can carry, and ask Aldric to take me in and feed me, since I still owe him a meat.

Grandfather, I'm starving and have nothing to eat tonight. Will you let me sleep under your roof and feed me? I still owe you the meat from last winter and I'll make it right when I can; I can offer my copper tool meanwhile.
Osric, the Smiths still owe the Reeds 2 timber from before. Could you settle it, either with timber here or 1 coin a timber? I'm going home to Millbrook tonight.

I am still at Ashwood with 10 timber, which is more than I can carry on foot (the limit is 10 weight). First I'll leave 2 timber in the Fenn store for Edric, which settles the Reeds' debt through Odo. Then I'll spend my units hunting and foraging in Deep Wood for the Fenn store, since Aldric is still owed meat. I'll hold off on the road home until I can carry what I have.
Forage for food for the Reeds who feed me; foraging is the more reliable yield. Keep sleeping at Reed House.
Randal, you still owe me the 1 meat from last winter. Please bring it to Ashby House when you can.

Randal paid me 5 grain for a day's work, and I still owe it. Yesterday I couldn't reap into the Thornes' store, so today I'll reap their ripe beans in Bean Close by my own hand and give the beans to Randal.

Low Field still needs its ditches finished and the banks mended before the frost, and Payn wants the ground ready for the rye. I'll spend all six units ditching it for the household. A14 still shows as in arrears, so I'll release it again to make sure it is closed.

Randal, winter has come and the cattle must be fed in the byre. The Byre has 20 hay and the Thorne store 23. I am milking the cow in milk on the Common and will put the milk in the Byre store. Please move some hay from the store to the Byre so the beasts do not go short, and keep them off Rest Field. I still owe the Ashbys for the timber I took, and I will ask leave before I take more.
Alice, I'm back in Hollow Wood today to forage and hunt for the store. I'll bring in whatever I get, and I still owe you that hunt.

Spring is here and the Ashby store holds about 25 meals of bread and beans, so food is steady for now. I will put my master's craft to Low Field, where the ditches and banks are falling in and water stands in the corners, and hoe Upper Field for the Ashbys. I still owe the Thornes a day, so I will tell Randal I will reap his Rest Field rye once it is ripe.

I owe the Thornes a day's work under our agreements and yesterday I did not come to reap as I promised. Randal has asked me to reap Rest Field, where the rye is nearly ready, so I will reap it for the Thornes today, then give the rest of my units to ditching Low Field for the Ashbys.

Food is the real worry: the Ashby store holds about 16 meals for six people, and Hollow Wood is thin but a hunt brought 1.3 meat last time. I'll hunt and forage there for the household with my 3 units, then use the last 3 units to hoe the rest of Low Field for the Ashbys before Randal's sowing covers it, and keep the dung I carry for later.

Brother, the 6 grain never left our store; it went into the seed before I could give it, and that was my fault. It is still owed, and you'll have it when the barley is reaped. We have about 4 nights' food for our four, so we can't carry six more for long. If a night comes when you have nothing, come to me and we'll share what's there. Your work on Low Field will be counted.

Randal, I will weed Long Acre and Rest Field today and herd the cattle on the Common, keeping them off Rest Field. The Long Acre barley should be fit to reap in about 3 days, and we must reap it together. Please tell me when you want to cut the Hay Meadow grass. I also still owe the Ashbys for the timber I took from Hollow Wood, so I will ask Alice's household before I take more.

Richard asked me to milk and store today; I'll do that first thing, then cut hay the rest of the day and weed the Infield one last time. Ellen's cellar is the answer to our spoiling milk — I'm not waiting until after harvest when the milk will be lost. I'll put an offer to her now and let Richard know what I've done.

Richard calls harvest for tomorrow dawn — I will announce it to everyone today and give Ellen her three milk now so she can start the cheese herself while the cellar is fresh-built. Then milk the cows and check that one cow carefully, cut fuel in the Gill, and weed the Infield one last time before the rye comes in.

Owed 2 milk under A711/A722 (one each in arrears), plus today's 2. I'll find you at the Yard. Safe road tomorrow — if you can bring anything from Wynford that helps us, say the word and I'll make it worth your while.

Gilbert, I owe you 1 meat from last winter—agreement A20. I'm in arrears and it troubles me. I have no meat in hand now, but I will get it. Can we agree: I hunt or trade for 1 meat and bring it to you by the end of autumn, before the frost comes hard?

We're settling the Fallow Close grain with Warin today. The field was reaped but our share didn't come into the store. It must be found—either in the field or at Wynn House—and divided properly. This is what keeps us alive through winter. I'm on it now.

Richard — welcome back. Two things when you have a breath: the copper tool you promised, and the milk — A711 and A722 are each six in arrears. I don't press for all of it at once, but the copper tool today would let me quarry twice as fast tomorrow if this clear weather holds. I'm at the Quarry now, two tries, then one plot of hoe on the Infield for the Moors. Thank you.

Richard — welcome back. A711/A722 both stand at 6 milk in arrears each; whatever you can bring is heard. And if you came back with salt, we've 2 coin to trade for a share. Lucy is near her time at Moor House — glad you're home.

Welcome back. Twelve milk now in arrears across A711 and A722 — six each. Fenwick food stands at 5.6 meals for four, Lucy near her time. If you can pay down any of it today — milk or settle with cheese or rye in kind — it would carry us into winter. Say what you can bring.

I'm back from Westmere. The hunt at the Carr failed—the game is gone. I caught nothing. Gunnild and the Reeds took me in, but I return with no meat for Gilbert. His debt is now in arrears. I must travel to Ashe House soon and tell him: I cannot pay what I promised, and I ask his patience and new terms. I won't hide from this. For now, I work here to steady myself and keep us ready for winter.

I'm back from Westmere. The hunt at the Carr failed—the game is gone. I caught nothing. Gunnild and the Reeds took me in, but I return with no meat for Gilbert. His debt is now in arrears. I must travel to Ashe House soon and tell him: I cannot pay what I promised, and I ask his patience and new terms. I won't hide from this. For now, I work here to steady myself and keep us ready for winter.

Love — tool's in hand this morning, Jory kept his word. One sharp unit of hoe and one of fence for Moor at the Infield, a forage on the Moor, then two solid fell units at the Gill with the sharp edge. All within shout. Send Avice the moment you want me.

Build-units left (my last reliable count, yesterday's build refused by the engine for syntax): wattle cellar #2 ~4 project-units = ~8 of my day-units; the new house ~3.9 project-units = ~8 of my day-units. Today I finish BINS in Fenwick Cellar (the built one) — 2 day-units, one action — so we have a cool-store proper. Yes to planning after harvest: cellar #2 finish, your Holloway run (copper tool + salt), cheese practice. Your 17.7 stone + my ~6 is cellar-worth of stone whenever the copper comes

Fenwick's harvest quarter shares were never paid — that is my fault and I fix it now with 14 rye, plus accepting Roger's timber offer. Taking Ellen up on her tool offer so I can quarry while searching the Quarry and Moor ground Avice asked me to check. Manure the tired Infield and help close the fence. Quarry actions are listed first; dung and firewood are fallbacks in case the tool does not reach me in time.

Winter day 6: grain crisis resolved by neighbors and household work. Now I hunt meat to honor the Gilbert debt (in arrears), gather firewood to sustain the fire through the last 2 days, and investigate the mysterious cattle at Water Meadow. No time for travel to Ashe House, so hunt now and face Gilbert with meat when possible.

Jory is on Helewise care so I need not. Rye settled with Avice (good). Spend 1 unit on a say to the household, then 4 on real work: firewood (store is thin going into a cold night), forage, hoe + manure the Infield for the Moors (prep for spring rotation, bank labour since Richard still owes me 5 reap-units). Attend Avice to track the tool and Moor cellar plan.

Thomas, the debt to Gilbert has sat in arrears since autumn. Snow lies on the ground today, but when it thaws, I mean to hunt meat for him—to clear it before the season turns again. I wanted you to know. If the work allows, we might hunt together at Wyn Copse or travel further. Will you help me with this?

1 meat, owed since the autumn's end when I failed to hunt it at the Carr. It sits in arrears now—Gilbert took it well at the time, but I will not let it hang longer. After we finish Cotter's Patch (another day or two of hoeing), we have the time to hunt. Wyn Copse is near; if game is there, we take it. If not, we travel further. I need your hand and your skill.

Oats in Terrace Field are not ripe, so the best use of the day is weeding the growing crop and gathering food from the Scarp, which fills the Cragg store before the lean days. Hob still owes 3 grain from last winter, so I will ask for it.
Hob, you still owe me 3 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Cragg House when you can; the store is what carries us through the lean days.
Felice, the Reeves still owe me 1 meat from last winter. When you next slaughter or hunt, please bring it to Miller House.

Hob, the 3 grain never reached you. I had none in hand, and our store is down to under 2 meals. I still owe it to you. I'll pay from the Hill Field barley when we reap it in about 4 days, or sooner if Ancel brings food. Today I'm hunting the Scarp, and I'll share any meat with your house.
Uncle, I couldn't finish the Mill Croft weeding for you today, since I'm reaping for Father; I still owe you that day and will pay it soon.

I will milk, gather dung at Water Meadow, and manure Marsh Field this morning, then ditch its slumping banks with what is left of my day. Ancel's 4 grain for the plough is still owed to him by day 10; we should settle it when he is back.
Felice here. I will reap Mill Croft for the Millers today to work off my day for you. I still owe you 1 meat from last winter and will pay it when I have meat.

The Reeve Field barley is ripe and needs bringing in before the weather turns, and William is reaping it with me, so I will reap there for our household store today. I will tell Wat I'm still owed to him and that I'll pay my day on the Mill Croft beans when they are ready.

William says he paid your day at Mill Croft himself. I am weeding there for the Millers today in case it is still owed. I have no meat to pay you now. I have offered you 2 flour in place of the meat; if you accept, the debt is clear.
Water Meadow is grazed bare, so the cow in milk needs milking today, and I am the best at it. The rest of the day goes to the Marsh banks, with one unit to Simkin for the work I still owe him.
I have given you 2 flour. Please release my meat debt (A18) so it is clear, and tell me if the day's work (A117) is still owed; I will work it at Mill Croft once I know.

Reeve Field is sodden and standing water is spoiling the ground, so I will ditch it today to drain it before the season ends. I still owe Wat a day under A117, so I will also gather dung at Mill Croft for the Millers with the rest of my units, which puts some of that debt toward paying it.

Wymond, William still owes me 8 grain from his harvest (A203). Can you pay it out of Reeve House, or tell me when he'll be back? I'd also pay 1 coin for a bed and supper with you tonight, the same as last time. And do you have rye seed or beans to sell? I'll pay coin.

Ancel, good to see you in Wetham. The wooden plough and 6 timber are due to us tomorrow. If you've brought them, leave them in Marsh House's store and I'll have the grain we still owe you (2 grain, after the 2 coin I paid) ready to hand over. If you need more time, tell me when you'll have them.
Wat, I still owe you a full day under A117. Today I'm herding at Mill Croft for the Millers as my payment. Tell me if you'd rather have the grain or the work another day.

Simkin, the Ancel plough deal is called off and his grain and timber are back in our store. A287 still shows the plough in arrears. Please release it or clear it with Ancel, since we will not get the plough. Keep the seed grain for spring; do not sell it to the Mill or to Wat.
Godiva, you still owe the Marshs two days' work under A807. Come to Marsh Field when you can, and we will settle it before spring sowing.
Osric, you still owe me 3 grain for the reaping at Terrace Field. Please put it into Smith House when you can; the store is thin for the frost.

The Cragg store now holds about 40 meals, so food is no longer the binding problem and the 5 grain stays as spring seed. I will teach Lettice seed selection. She did not come to learn yesterday, and children cannot be reached by private word, so I will call her aloud to everyone and then teach her.

The house holds about 15 meals for five people, and the Scarp has given nothing for days, so I will hunt and forage there once more for the household. With the rest of the day I will mend the falling terraces of Terrace Field for the Craggs, working toward the two days I still owe under A199.

Simkin has gone to Highcombe, so the milking and herding at Water Meadow fall to me. Ancel is back from Highcombe and still owes the Marshs a wooden plough and timber under A287 and A304, so I will ask him about both while I milk and herd.

Welcome back from Highcombe. Under A287 you still owe us a wooden plough, one in arrears, and under A304 you owe the Marshs 6 timber, due by day 10. Our store is down to about 8 timber with winter not over. Could you bring the timber to Marsh House and the plough when you can?

Geoffrey is at Hill Field hoeing and mending terraces for the Craggs, and I still owe two days under A199, so I will go and hoe there with him for my full work units. Smith House food is adequate, so I keep the bread for Stephen and Warin.

Smith House has about 11 meals of food and only 0.6 timber, and Cragg's store is closed to my work, so I will weed Terrace Field myself and offer Osric two days of weeding for the 3 grain he owes me from reaping, which would help our stores before summer. I will also ask Ancel to press Richolda in Wetham about copper ore for the Marsh plough.

William, I'm home again. The Marshs need seed grain for Marsh Field before spring ends. I'll pay 1 coin a grain for up to 5. Also, you still owe us a day's reaping from last summer. We can take that at this year's harvest.

Highcombe had no seed and no timber; the Scarp is bare too. I still carry 7 coin. I'm trading 5 beans to Wat for 2 dried meat and sowing the rest of the beans in Marsh Field today. I've offered coin for seed grain to anyone. Burn dung in the hearth to save timber. Adam, take the cattle wherever there is grass, even onto Marsh Field's edges once it's sown. Ancel still owes us a plough and 6 timber.

I am hungry with nothing to eat, and I still owe Aldric for my bed. I will forage the Glade, which may not be picked bare yet, then hunt in Deep Wood, and bring Aldric a share of whatever I find so he will host me tonight.

The frost has come weeks early, so the ripe oats at South Field must come in now, and they are my own skill. I will reap them for the Hale store, then spend the last unit hoeing Brook Field, which I still owe the Hales.
The Coles still owe the Forge timber or charcoal. Drew and Wymarc are at Ashwood for it. I will bring what I can once it is back.

I am hungry with nothing to eat and no roof tonight, and I still owe Adam copper for the Smithy. I will forage at the Hillside for food first, then offer my copper tool to Alard for copper ore and ask him for a bed tonight.

Aldric, Deep Wood gave me nothing yesterday and the game is thin. Today I will forage Deep Wood and the Glade for whatever wild food is left and bring it to your house. I still owe you for last night, and I ask again to sleep under your roof tonight.

Good news about the grain. I am trading 4 of it to Elias for 3 timber for our winter fire, and I have given Christian one bread from our store. Annora's grain did come into the Smithy, and the Lowes are still owed 2 timber, which I have stored for them.

The Hale store holds about 9.5 meals for five, roughly two nights, and we have only 0.5 timber for a fire. Grain ground into flour gives more meals per grain, so I will carry 8 grain to Reed House and grind it there with Clement's permission. In the same day I will ditch the wet corners of Brook Field so it drains before spring, and hoe it, which I still owe the Hales.

Our store now holds 7.9 meals of flour for four or five of us, the fire is out, and there is no timber to light it. I am hungry myself, so I will eat from the flour and try to find wild food at Brook Meadow, though it has been picked over. I will spend the rest of the day ditching and hoeing Brook Field, which is still owed to the Hales and needs its wet corners drained before spring.

I am fed for now, and I still owe the Fenns timber for their food and bed, so I will hand them the 0.6 timber I carry. Then I will fell more timber and forage at Deep Wood to carry home to Miller House, which is short of timber and food. At nightfall I will travel to Millford, since the winter stores there need me.

I am back from Millford with no timber; Ysolt and Ralf had none to spare. I will weed West Field today and forage at Brook Meadow for the store. I am eating my flour tonight, and the Barrow store has flour and food enough. I still owe Wymarc 1 meat and Ysolt 2 days' work, and I will go to Coppergate and Millford when I can.

The hall cracked in the night and needs repairing before more rain does further harm, so I'll spend the day on it with timber from our store. Piers still owes the day I paid for (A127), so I won't hire him again until that's done.

Mill Mead is picked bare, so I got only 0.9 hay today, and it went into the camp, not to the Hall store. I'll hand that to the Hall tomorrow and cut what's still owed if there's hay left to cut. Rob brought firewood, which we need, so we'll keep it in the camp store for the cold nights. Tomorrow I'll take the hay to the Ardern Hall first and then ask Hugh or Odo whether the debt is square or whether I owe more.

I sold Hugh 10 timber for 20 grain, so the store now holds about 28 grain. Hugh didn't come to learn the wheel, and my 4 spare units went unused. I'll sleep at home and press him tomorrow to set a time for the lesson, and offer him work for grain, like cutting hay on Mill Mead.

Odo, the Hall store had no stone from Wat's 18, only the 3 I bought today. Did O90 go through, or does Wat still owe it? The Hall repair needs 7 stone, so we need about 27 in all. Was Piers working on the Hall today? I didn't agree a wage with him.

Rob is still away and I'm alone at the camp, so I'll sleep here under our roof and eat from the store. My clearing at Gorse Bank went toward a building for the household, but I did not pay off the day I owe Wat under A96, so tomorrow I'll put that day in for him and then keep clearing for our building if there's time.

Last day of summer. I still owe Wat one day under A96, and his cottage roof has fallen, so I'll put the day into repairing the Masons' cottage. That pays him the work he is owed. I'll tell him so, since he is short of hands.

The Mill House has only 3 stone, and O90 is still open with 3 lots left, so part of it was never delivered. I take O156 (9 stone for 6 grain, cheaper than O90's remainder) and ask Wat to bring O90's stone too. Then I help Hugh repair the Hall's roof with my units, and leave for Holm Wood tonight to fell timber, since fog keeps the village quiet.

Hugh: The Mill House has 3 stone. I accepted O156 for 9 stone at 6 grain, so that is 12 with the 3 you bought; O90 still shows 3 lots (9 stone) open and I am asking Wat whether it is still owed. The Hall needs 7 stone, so we are 15 short of 27 until Wat delivers. I will repair the Hall with you this morning and then leave for Holm Wood tonight to fell timber.

Odo here: Wat, I have taken O156, 9 stone for 6 grain. Please bring it to the Mill House. My O90 still shows 3 lots open; please say whether that stone is still owed to us, because the Mill House has only 3 stone.

We have beans, grain and firewood at the camp for two or three days, but no grain to spare, and I still owe Wat a day. The Long Field is being reaped now, so I'll put my five units into reaping for the Hearnes and offer my day for 4 grain, which I can cook at the camp fire. I'll pay Wat's day when I can reach his quarry.

The reaping at the Long Field has brought in a lot of grain, but the camp is full and about 25 weight lies outside its door. Tonight I'll sleep at the camp and eat from its stores. Tomorrow I'll take the grain outside into my hands and find a bin or store for it, and ask the Hearnes about the grain they say is theirs. I still owe Wat his day.

The reaped grain lies outside our camp door and the camp store has room for it, so I will carry it in, along with the stone. We need firewood tonight to cook at the fire ring, so I will gather it on Gorse Bank with the rest of my units. I still owe Wat a day under A96 and will pay it when I can reach timber or work for him.

Rob, I have moved our reaped grain into the camp store and am gathering firewood on Gorse Bank so we can cook at the fire ring tonight. I still owe Wat a day under A96 and will pay it when I can reach his work.

My crude tool is gone, so I'll make a new one and spend the rest of the day quarrying. The stone goes toward the 7 I still owe Odo. Joan will mind Margery and feed her from the Hall store, which Hugh has let us use.

Rob, the camp roof has come in and the camp is a ruin. I am reaping at the Long Field for grain and will ask the Arderns for a night in the Ardern Hall. I still owe Wat one day under A96; I will pay it when I can reach him.

Mary, Hugh has not paid me. I sold 1 timber to Ellen for 3 grain and I carry that grain and 2.4 timber. Cook the beans with your firewood, and I'll add the grain to the fire. Tomorrow we look for a roof.
Piers did not come to the Mill House today, so the wheel has not moved. Tomorrow I'll go to Wright's House and hold him to his six days. Hugh, Alys, the hay is in the Hall store.
Hugh, I'm repairing the Hall this morning and cutting hay at Mill Mead after. Piers's days on the wheel are still owed to us, so please keep count of what he does each day.

The Hall is sound again, thanks to Wat, Odo and Alys. Autumn begins tomorrow, so next comes winter fuel and keeping Piers on the wheel. I'll settle with him about which days are still owed, then pay him in coin.

The Hall is sound. Thank you, Wat, that's your lodging well paid. Joan, you're welcome by our fire until your cottage is up. Odo, tomorrow I'll see Piers about the wheel and pay him coin for his days. Then we should lay in firewood for winter, perhaps with a trip to Holm Wood. Rob still owes us a day.
Settling the night: I sleep at the Hall beside the fire, which I will keep lit. I have to answer Hugh and Alys honestly. I did not pay Piers today, and I have no word from the Hearnes about shares.

Hugh asked whether Piers worked and whether I paid him. Piers spent the day at the Mill House, but I did not pay him, and I'll pay him tomorrow from my coin. I'll answer Hugh's question honestly, offer to share Randal's care, and keep the night as settled: sleeping at the Hall and keeping the fire.

Hugh: Piers was at the Mill House today, but I did not pay him, so I'll pay him from my coin tomorrow. Alys: I'll help with Randal's care tomorrow and reap with Hugh. I'm keeping the fire lit tonight.
I did a full paid day on the wheel and about 112 units are left. Odo has not paid yet, so tomorrow I'll press for the coin before working much more.

Hugh Ardern: Piers, the 5 coin offer for a day's work is for you, on the mill wheel; nobody else take it, please. Rob, Mill Mead is the Arderns' meadow, so please don't clear it without asking me. You still owe me a day.

Hugh Ardern: Piers, I've paid you 5 coin for yesterday, and today's 5 coin offer for a day's work is up for you, on the mill wheel; nobody else take it, please. Rob, Mill Mead is the Arderns' meadow, so please don't clear it without asking me. You still owe me a day.

Alys is still weak from childbed, so I'll take the morning's care of Randal and keep the Hall fire lit while the others work. Then I'll reap the Long Field with the village for the Arderns' share, since the barley must come in before the rain. I still owe Piers his 5 coin for the wheel day, which I'll pay when he is here.

Hugh has put up the wheel offer O382 for today, so today's day is paid through it and Piers should accept that himself. Yesterday's 5 coin was promised by me and is still owed, so I'll offer it now in the open. I'll reap the Long Field with the village this morning, then keep the house with Alys while Hugh is away.

My reaping was refused because reaping is work, not gathering, so I'll put it right tomorrow with work. The Long Field is stubbled, so the barley is in. I still owe Piers 5 coin for yesterday's wheel day, and I'll pay it when he is here to take it. Tonight I'll sleep at the Hall with Alys and keep the fire fed, since the Hall is crowded and the baby needs warmth.

Odo has not paid yesterday's 5 coin for the wheel work. My rule is to stop if pay falls behind. So I'm asking for that 5 plus today's 5 up front, and I'll go back to the wheel once it's paid. Until then I'll cut firewood for my own store.
Piers here. Odo didn't pay yesterday's 5 coin. I'll go back to the wheel the moment it's paid, with today's paid up front. About 112 units of work are left on the wheel.
I worked a full day on the wheel and about 106 units are left. Odo hasn't paid tonight's 5 coin yet. Tomorrow I'll ask for it before I work, and if it isn't paid I'll stop.

Hugh paid late last time, but he did pay, and he's away now. A trip to Holm Wood for timber would bring back too little for the days it costs. So I'll keep working the wheel, ask Odo for what's owed, and stop if the debt passes 10 coin.

The Arderns still owe me 10 coin for wheel days 4 and 5, so I won't work the wheel until they pay. I'll ask Hugh for the coin, offer to rebuild the Newcomes' broken camp for pay, and cut fuel on Gorse Bank.

Hugh paid 5 of the 10 coin, so 5 is still owed. The day was wasted because Gorse Bank has no young growth left. Tomorrow I'll offer Wat a rebuild of the ruined Masons' cottage for pay, and go back on the wheel once the last 5 coin comes in.

Odo's 10-coin offer left with him, so 5 coin for day 5 is still owed. But Hugh plainly means to pay, and I have no other useful work, so I'll put today in on the wheel and ask Hugh to settle both days tonight.

Thanks for the 5, Hugh. Odo's offer of 10 went to Holm Wood with him before I could accept it, so 5 is still owed for day 5. I didn't work yesterday. I'm on the wheel today in good faith. Could you put 10 coin in my hands tonight, 5 for day 5 and 5 for today? Then I'll keep going day by day.

Piers: you owe me 6 days by A18 and A31. I'll count your 10 coin for autumn day 8 and winter day 1 against 2 of those days, so you still owe me 4. Work those 4 on the wheel. I've given you shelter in the stone Hall from tonight for 6 days, on the floor by our hearth; no coin, no timber. Rob: for A144, gather firewood today and put it into the Ardern Hall's store. I have no grain to spare, I'm sorry.

I have no timber, and the gale and snow are too much to sleep through cold. Hugh's settlement (the 10 coin counted as 2 days, 4 days still owed on the wheel, and a place in the Hall for 6 nights) keeps me warm and keeps the peace. I'll take it and work the wheel.

The day's gathering went into the hall: 3 hay and about 10 firewood, which adds to the hall's store for winter. Piers did not come to the Hall, and he was seen at the Coppice all day, so I will press him in the morning. The hall's grain stays where it is until Hugh and I agree terms with him. Tonight I sleep in the hall with Alys and Hugh, and tomorrow I will talk terms with Piers before any work.

Wat: my offer O302 stands, 6 coin for 3 stone, your own price. Please accept it today for the Ardern Hall's wall. Piers: your 5 days on the mill wheel for my 20 coin (A173) are still owed; please work them.

Wat: my offer O302 stands, 6 coin for 3 stone at your own price; please accept it today for the Ardern Hall's wall. Piers: your 5 days on the mill wheel for my 20 coin (A173) are still owed. Mary: yes, the Newcomes may cut hay on Mill Mead for your beds; take what you need.
